injuryReports.name: Jon Gaines II
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Carson Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Devin Duvernay
injuryReports.returnComment: Duvernay played two offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver took a step back after three targets in Week 10, leaving the Week 11 wide receiver action to Simi Fehoko and Harrison Wallace.
injuryReports.injury: Duvernay logged 81 kick return yards in the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Virgil
injuryReports.returnComment: The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season. He's never been relevant in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Virgil wasn't targeted in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cardinals offense struggled Sunday with Josh Johnson as the starter in the absence of Carson Beck (back). Of Johnson's 31 pass attempts, 26 of them were split between Trey McBride (14), Harrison Wallace (seven) and Simi Fehoko (five), leaving very little for Higgins and the other Cardinals pass catchers. Higgins has only one catch over his last two outings and a 19-166-1 receiving line on 21 targets through 11 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins caught his lone target for four yards during the Cardinal' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Simi Fehoko
injuryReports.returnComment: The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.
injuryReports.injury: Fehoko caught one of five targets for a two-yard touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Zay Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.
injuryReports.injury: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Harrison Wallace III
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie emerged with a 4-57-0 line on seven targets against the Chiefs, with the targets, receptions and yards all pacing Arizona wideouts. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Wallace finished Sunday's loss to Kansas City with four catches for 57 yards on seven targets.

injuryReports.name: Chad Ryland
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing with their third- and fourth-string quarterbacks, the Cardinals have mustered a total of 13 points over their last two games. Ryland has minimal fantasy appeal in an offense struggling to simply move the ball. On the season, he's 22-for-24 on field-goal tries and 17-for-18 on PATs across 11 games.
injuryReports.injury: Ryland made his lone extra-point attempt in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Jeremiyah Love
injuryReports.returnComment: "I'll know a little bit more as this week goes," LaFleur noted of Love, who will miss at least one more game before potentially being activated ahead of, and available for, Week 13 action. Love sustained a right high-ankle sprain Nov. 1, and at the time he was thought to be facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. However, for this coming weekend's game against the Commanders at least, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to handle Arizona's backfield duties.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Teagan Quitoriano
injuryReports.returnComment: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.
injuryReports.injury: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Hunter Long
injuryReports.returnComment: Long ranked third among Cardinals tight ends in playing time, logging 23 of 56 offensive snaps while Trey McBride (45 snaps) and Elijah Higgins (32) paced the position group. In his first two contests back in action since being reinstated from injured reserve Nov. 14 following a five-game absence, Long has notched two receptions for 18 yards on three targets.
injuryReports.injury: Long hauled in his lone target for an 11-yard reception in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Bam Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: Although he split the backfield workload nearly equally with Tyler Allgeier, Knight was the more productive RB, although he still failed to reach 50 rushing yards for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old running back gets a more favorable matchup in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Knight and Allgeier could face additional competition for touches if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is cleared to return.
injuryReports.injury: Knight carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Allgeier
injuryReports.returnComment: Game script fairly quickly put the Cardinals' running game in mothballs, and Allgeier wound up splitting the backfield workload nearly equally with Bam Knight, who picked up 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Allgeier has gone three straight games without reaching 50 rushing yards or getting into the end zone, but those games were also against very tough opponents (the Seahawks in Week 9 and the Rams in Week 10). The fifth-year RB could find a little more running room in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Jeremiyah Love (ankle) might also be ready to rejoin the lineup by then.
injuryReports.injury: Allgeier carried the ball seven times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.

injuryReports.name: Josh Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: The 40-year-old QB was pressed into duty with rookie Carson Beck (back) on the shelf, and Johnson unsurprisingly wasn't really up to the task after the Cardinals fell into a 14-0 hole before the first quarter was over. Johnson spent most of his afternoon finding Trey McBride for short gains, and he did hit Simi Fehoko for a two-yard score in the second quarter. Beck doesn't figure to miss much time, but if Johnson gets another start in Week 12, he'll be taking on a much less formidable Commanders defense.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. he added five yards on two carries.

injuryReports.name: Trey McBride
injuryReports.returnComment: Working with his fourth quarterback of the season in Josh Johnson, McBride dominated the 40-year-old's attention, as no other Cardinal got more than seven targets or hauled in more than four passes. The star tight end wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, as his longest gain went for a mere nine yards. Carson Beck (back) could be back under center in Week 12 against the Commanders, but that might not improve McBride's outlook, as he saw only five targets in Week 10 during the rookie QB's first NFL start.
injuryReports.injury: McBride caught nine of 14 targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. He added four yards on his only carry.

injuryReports.name: Cody Simon
injuryReports.returnComment: Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Hjalte Froholdt
injuryReports.returnComment: Froholdt was a full practice participant both Thursday and Friday, and he's progressed enough in his recovery to clear the league's concussion protocol. With Jon Gaines (ankle) ruled out, Froholdt should reclaim his starting job at center for Sunday's road tilt.
injuryReports.injury: Froholdt (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Zachary Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury he picked up in training camp in early August. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 11 prep but is not quite ready to return, so his next chance to make his 2026 debut is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jayden Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams appears ready to return after missing the previous two games. He's been working as the Cardinals' starting left tackle after Paris Johnson (biceps) went on injured reserve following Week 4.
injuryReports.injury: Williams (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Walter Nolen III
injuryReports.returnComment: The defensive tackle was not able to practice Wednesday due to an illness. Now that he's back, he should be able to play Sunday against the Chiefs. Nolen has played on a majority of the defensive snaps in each game he's been available for this season, recording 25 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks.
injuryReports.injury: Nolen (illness) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Divine Deablo
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Forearm

injuryReports.name: Zachariah Branch
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: DeMarcco Hellams
injuryReports.returnComment: Hellams racked up tackles in what ended up being a disastrous night for the Falcons' defense. It's typically not a good thing when your third-level defender has to make all the plays, but make them, Hellams did, saving several explosive plays from the Chiefs' offense from becoming house calls.
injuryReports.injury: Hellams logged 11 tackles (seven solo) in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Olamide Zaccheaus
injuryReports.returnComment: Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.

injuryReports.name: Jahan Dotson
injuryReports.returnComment: Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. He's fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. Dotson isn't a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Jake Moody
injuryReports.returnComment: Moody was signed by the Falcons off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, and he was able to put together a perfect debut with the team in Week 10. The kicker converted a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter before later adding a 38-yard make in the fourth. With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Moody went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Austin Hooper
injuryReports.returnComment: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.
injuryReports.injury: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.

injuryReports.name: Drake London
injuryReports.returnComment: London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Michael Penix Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Bijan Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Kendal Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Daniels popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an Achilles injury, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's home game. The rookie fourth-rounder has accumulated 61 tackles (41 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: C.J. Henderson
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network, Henderson's extension is worth up to $20 million and includes $11 million guaranteed. Henderson has started at outside cornerback in each of his last six outings, and he was moved into the starting lineup after A.J. Terrell landed on injured reserve in late September due to a groin injury. Across eight regular-season games, Henderson has logged 41 tackles (32 solo), nine pass defenses, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Henderson and the Falcons agreed to a two-year contract extension Friday.

injuryReports.name: Cameron Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: The extension means Thomas -- a third-round selection of the Cardinals in the 2022 NFL Draft -- will be under contract with the Falcons through the 2029 season. The fifth-year pro has stepped into a larger role defensively this year due to the absences of James Pearce (back) and Jalon Walker (knee, IR), the former of whom missed the first eight games of the 2026 campaign while serving a suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Thomas has accumulated 25 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Thomas and the Falcons agreed to a three-year extension worth up to $33 million Friday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Vorhees
injuryReports.returnComment: The move gives the Falcons additional depth at the guard position behind starters Chris Lindstrom and Matthew Bergeron. Vorhees -- a seventh-round selection of the Ravens in the 2023 NFL Draft -- started in all 17 regular-season games in 2025, but he's started in only two of five contests this year. He also missed two games in October while recovering from a foot injury.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens traded Vorhees and a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the Falcons on Tuesday in exchange for Ryan Neuzil, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Nnamdi Madubuike
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Roquan Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith has at least eight tackles in 10 of 11 games this season but has just two games of double-digit tackles. On the season, the veteran linebacker has piled up 91 tackles (40 solo), including 2.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and two forced fumbles on 94 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Smith recorded nine tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cuevas
injuryReports.returnComment: Cuevas continues to draw targets at an impressive clip, tallying three for his second straight game despite only being on the field for 14 of the Ravens' 61 offensive snaps in Week 11. Barring an injury to starter Mark Andrews or rookie fourth-rounder Matt Hibner, though, his role isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats. Baltimore will take on the Texans in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Cuevas caught one of three targets for eight yards during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
injuryReports.returnComment: Lane failed to reel in a pass for the second time in three weeks, and both times the ball was thrown his way Sunday, the play was negated by a defensive penalty, resulting in no targets for the rookie. Lane was on the field for 33 offensive snaps, ranking third at wide receiver for Baltimore behind Rashod Bateman (59) and Zay Flowers (57). Lane's next chance to get back on track will come in Week 12 against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Lane didn't garner a target during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Devontez Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: The wide receiver took on the role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he can perhaps find his place on the return team.
injuryReports.injury: Walker recorded 211 kickoff-return yards, including an 86-yard touchdown, and one catch for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Riley Patterson
injuryReports.returnComment: Patterson was able to convert his only field-goal try in Week 11, nailing a chip-shot 28-yard attempt in the first quarter. Patterson has now combined to go 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts while making all six of his PATs over two contests as the starting kicker for Baltimore, and he will likely remain in that role for Week 12 with Tyler Loop (groin) sidelined for at least one more contest.
injuryReports.injury: Patterson made his only field-goal attempt and went 4-for-4 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Marlon Humphrey
injuryReports.returnComment: The Ravens sent Humphrey home Thursday and made him a healthy inactive for this past Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers after he made a negative comment about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. Though Humphrey is expected to be a full participant in practice throughout Week 12, Minter suggested that he'll determine at the end of the week whether he wants to make the 30-year-old cornerback available Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Matt Hibner
injuryReports.returnComment: Hibner logged 35 of 65 snaps on offense, with his 54 percent share ranking second to only Mark Andrews (62 percent) among Ravens tight ends. The rookie fourth-round pick out of SMU's playing time has held steady between 30 and 60 percent of snaps over his 10 appearances, with Hibner drawing no more than two targets in any of those contests.
injuryReports.injury: Hibner recorded two catches for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Rashod Bateman
injuryReports.returnComment: The wideout's big play was a 52-yard touchdown strike from Jacoby Brissett in the first quarter. It was Bateman's first score since Week 2, and his 67 yards were his second-most in a game this season. Bateman has three or fewer catches in six straight contests and isn't someone to chase in fantasy ahead of next Sunday's date with the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Bateman recorded two catches for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Mark Andrews
injuryReports.returnComment: While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Andrews caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Justice Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Derrick Henry had a strong performance as well but was knocked out of the game in the fourth quarter and got checked for a concussion. Hill was heavily involved in the offense prior to that, however, scoring from 19 yards out in the late in the second quarter. He almost had a second TD earlier in the quarter, but Hill had the ball punched loose at the one-yard line after a 36-yard scamper and saw it bounce out of the end zone for a turnover and a touchback. Henry cleared the concussion protocol after the game and figures to be active in the Week 12 against the Texans, but Hill's usage appears to be on the upswing as the Ravens' No. 2 back.
injuryReports.injury: Hill carried the ball six times for 69 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Jacoby Brissett
injuryReports.returnComment: It was another decent showing for the veteran quarterback, and his first TD pass in two games as a Raven came on a trick that involved a direct snap to Derrick Henry, who flipped it Brissett for a 52-yard strike to Rashod Bateman. Brissett has also kept Zay Flowers relevant, feeding the wideout 18 targets for a 14-171-0 line. Baltimore's passing attack will try to keep improving in Week 12 against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Brissett completed 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers. He added seven rushing yards on two carries.

injuryReports.name: Zay Flowers
injuryReports.returnComment: No other Raven caught more than four passes or saw more than six targets as Flowers continues to build chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The fourth-year wideout has posted a 14-171-0 line on 18 targets in Brissett's first two starts for Baltimore, immediately establishing a strong floor. Flowers will try to keep rolling in Week 12 against what has been a surprisingly vulnerable Texans defense.
injuryReports.injury: Flowers caught eight of 11 targets for 97 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.

injuryReports.name: Derrick Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: Henry was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of the contest, but evidently passed all tests. Prior to his exit, Henry carried 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and hauled in four of his five targets for 17 yards. He also lost his second fumble of the season. Henry looks like he'll be ready to handle his normal role as the lead option out of the Baltimore backfield next Sunday against the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Henry cleared concussion protocol and was made available to the media following Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers, Giana Han of the Baltimore Banner reports.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Sarratt
injuryReports.returnComment: Sarratt has been active for two games this season, most recently appearing in Week 4 versus the Titans. Since then, he's been held out. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 versus the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Sarratt (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Adam Randall
injuryReports.returnComment: Randall was recently reinstated from injured reserve. However, with Derrick Henry, Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali available versus the Panthers, Randall will be inactive.
injuryReports.injury: Randall (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina.

injuryReports.name: Olaivavega Ioane
injuryReports.returnComment: The offensive guard was limited during Wednesday's session. Ioane left Monday's loss to the Chargers with a shoulder injury and didn't return. The first-round pick out of Penn State has started all nine games he's played in this season.
injuryReports.injury: Ioane (shoulder/knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.

injuryReports.name: Rasheen Ali
injuryReports.returnComment: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: Lamar Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamilton is managing a hip injury but played all but one of Baltimore's defensive snaps Monday. He led the team with 10 stops, which were the second-most he's recorded in a contest so far this season. Hamilton seems to be on his way to a third consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign, as he has 70 stops through 10 games on the season.
injuryReports.injury: Hamilton posted 10 tackles (three solo) against the Chargers in Monday's Week 10 loss.

injuryReports.name: Mike Green
injuryReports.returnComment: Green's first sack came late in the second quarter, and he brought down Chargers QB Justin Herbert again early in the fourth. After registering 3.5 sacks in 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, Green has already exceeded that mark with 5.5 sacks through 10 contests this season. His six total tackles in Week 10 also tied his career-high mark.
injuryReports.injury: Green racked up six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers.

injuryReports.name: T.J. Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Amani Hooker
injuryReports.returnComment: Hooker has now played in two games for the Bills, logging 100 percent of the team's defensive reps in Week 11 and 98 percent in Week 12. The strong safety has made for a good pairing with Cole Bishop, and the duo has helped the Bills' defense extend its streak of not allowing a touchdown to 15 straight quarters of play.
injuryReports.injury: Hooker logged two solo tackles and one pass defensed in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Terrel Bernard
injuryReports.returnComment: Bernard had his lowest output of the season in Sunday's contest. The linebacker played 28 defensive snaps, on just 62 percent of the team's defensive plays. The defensive captain was likely pulled early to rest for Thursday night's primetime game against the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Bernard logged two tackles (one solo) in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tyrell Shavers
injuryReports.returnComment: Shavers played 27 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams in his return to the field Sunday. The wide receiver has finally started to mix into the offense after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in the Bills' 27-24 win over the Jaguars in the 2025 AFC wild-card round.
injuryReports.injury: Shavers was targeted twice for zero catches and logged one tackle on kick coverage in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ty Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson did not carry the rock much at all in the contest. The running back did however rank third in Buffalo receiving yards behind Khalil Shakir (101) and DJ Moore (91).  Johnson should continue to see receiving opportunities in Week 12 against the Chiefs as the Bills' preferred third-down back.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson rushed once for two yards and caught seven of his eight targets for 55 yards in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dorian Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams did not play in Sunday's win over the Dolphins due to a calf injury that kept him out of all Week 11 prep. The inside linebacker's estimated presence Monday is promising, but he will likely need to suit up for on-field practice Tuesday and Wednesday to get the green light ahead of Thursday night's Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Greg Rousseau
injuryReports.returnComment: Rousseau had another 2.0 sack game against the Dolphins on Sunday. The linebacker now has four such games this season, and his 10.0 sacks in 10 games have already surpassed his previous single-season total of 8.0. The 26-year-old picked up a back injury in the dominant win and will likely need to practice both Tuesday and Wednesday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Christian Benford
injuryReports.returnComment: The cornerback sat out of Sunday's win over the Dolphins after exiting the previous week's victory over the Jets with the injury. Buffalo still has two more practices this week ahead of Thursday night's clash with Kansas City, but Benford is not on track to play at this point. If he can't go, Tre'Davious White, Jordan Hancock and Maxwell Hairston could be in line to see more snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Damar Hamlin
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Spencer Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: O'Cyrus Torrence
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuryReports.returnComment: Kincaid didn't practice at all last week before being made inactive for Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins. Though the Bills didn't actually practice Monday, Kincaid's 'limited' listing does represent an upgrade and suggests that the tight end has a chance to be available for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs. Further context regarding his Week 12 status is set to arrive via Tuesday's practice report, in any case.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Keleki Latu
injuryReports.returnComment: With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) inactive, Latu moved a rung up on the ladder at tight end and ended up seeing his most extensive playing time on offense of the season, logging 28 of 78 snaps (36 percent). He parlayed the elevated snaps into a season-high target count, but Latu's lone reception actually came on special teams, when Tommy Doman faked a punt and connected with the 24-year-old deep down the field for a fourth-down conversion. Latu will likely see his opportunities take a hit if Kincaid makes it back for a Thursday matchup with the Chiefs in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Latu recorded a 30-yard reception on four targets in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Bass
injuryReports.returnComment: Bass was able to make at least three field goals for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The kicker made field goals from 43 and 54 yards in the first half before adding makes from 40 and 28 yards in the fourth quarter. His lone miss of the day came in the third quarter, when he pulled a 54-yard try wide left, registering his first missed field-goal try of the year. Bass has now gone 24-for-25 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-5 from 50-plus yards, over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Bass went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Keon Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: Coleman finished with fewer than 20 receiving yards for the fourth straight week, and he hasn't reached the end zone since Week 6. The wide receiver has operated in a limited role on offense since DJ Moore returned to action in Week 8 following a shoulder injury, and Coleman will remain an unattractive fantasy asset ahead of the team's matchup with the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman caught two of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 26-9 win over Miami.

injuryReports.name: Ray Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with the Bills having a quick Week 12 turnaround ahead of Thursday night's game against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, Buffalo rode James Cook and handed him 22 carries rather than spelling him a little more ahead of a short week. Davis has handled 17 carries across 10 games this season, turning them into a measly 55 yards and no touchdowns. His only fantasy value is being Cook's backup.
injuryReports.injury: Davis rushed one time for three yards and caught a six-yard pass on two targets in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Dawson Knox
injuryReports.returnComment: Knox was the top available TE for the Bills in the absence of Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle). The added opportunities helped Knox post his second-highest total of the season in receiving yards, but Knox remains off the radar in most fantasy formats heading into Thursday's game against the Chiefs. He hasn't scored since Week 2 while recording a meager 117 yards on 16 catches through 10 games.
injuryReports.injury: Knox caught two of three targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Shakir
injuryReports.returnComment: Shakir led the Bills in receiving yards in the absence of TE Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle), posting 10 more than DJ Moore, who had one more target than Shakir. Sunday marked Shakir's first time reaching the 100-yard threshold since a 110-yard showing in Week 12 of last season. Shakir will look to build on this outing as he searches for his second TD of the season Thursday against the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Shakir caught five of nine targets for 101 yards while rushing twice for two yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: DJ Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore's four-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter gave him his first multi-game regular-season touchdown streak since Weeks 15 and 16 of the 2025 campaign with the Bears. He briefly left the game later in the first half to have his knee looked at but promptly returned and ultimately reached the 90-yard threshold for a second consecutive game while leading the team in targets. Barring a setback with his knee on a short week, Moore should continue to work as Buffalo's top wide receiver Thanksgiving night against the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Moore caught eight of 10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: James Cook III
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. He accounted for all but five of Buffalo's rushing attempts as Josh Allen finished without one, but Cook came up short of 100 scrimmage yards for the first time since Week 4. The reigning NFL rushing yards leader continues to put up stellar production heading into Thursday night's home game against the Chiefs.
injuryReports.injury: Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Josh Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen threw a four-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore in the second quarter but got picked off twice later in the first half and had a would-be third interception nullified by a penalty on the penultimate play before halftime. Despite some sloppy play and zero rushing production from Allen, the 9-1 Bills cruised past the 1-9 Dolphins as the star QB raised his season total to 25 touchdowns (14 passing, 11 rushing). Buffalo's likely to encounter more resistance Thursday night against the 8-2 Chiefs. Allen is 5-1 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season but 0-4 when they face off in the playoffs.
injuryReports.injury: Allen completed 27 of 45 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Ed Oliver
injuryReports.returnComment: Oliver popped up on the injury report after informing the team's medical staff of oblique pain and was listed as questionable. However, the veteran is cleared to play for Sunday's divisional meeting with Miami, potentially resulting in fewer snaps for DeWayne Carter, Greg Gaines and Landon Jackson.
injuryReports.injury: Oliver (oblique) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Jackson Hawes
injuryReports.returnComment: Hawes was in danger of missing this contest due to a shoulder issue, though he will avoid his first absence of the 2026 campaign Sunday versus Miami. With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) sidelined in Week 11, Hawes will have an opportunity to get more involved than usual behind Dawson Knox.
injuryReports.injury: Hawes (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

injuryReports.name: Bobby Okereke
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Devin Lloyd
injuryReports.returnComment: The four tackles matched Lloyd's season low in a game this season, which he's done three times in nine contests. While he doesn't post huge tackle numbers, Lloyd makes noise in other areas of the box score. He's piled up 67 tackles (39 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and five pass breakups, including three interceptions, on 94 percent of the defensive snaps in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Lloyd recorded four tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Legette
injuryReports.returnComment: The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Legette did not play an offensive snap in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Tommy Tremble
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end played on 82 percent of the offensive snaps but only saw one target. Tremble has 36 targets across 10 appearances this season, recording 26 catches for 245 yards and three scores.
injuryReports.injury: Tremble caught one pass for 18 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: John Metchie III
injuryReports.returnComment: Metchie and Bryce Young connected on a 19-yard pass late in the third quarter to set the Panthers up in the red zone, and the drive ended four plays later on a 33-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. Metchie has caught one pass in each of his last two outings, and the fifth-year pro is firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker on the wide receiver depth chart. The Panthers will hit the road in Week 12 for a crucial NFC South clash against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Metchie caught one of three targets for 19 yards during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Trevor Etienne
injuryReports.returnComment: Etienne did it all in Week 11 while only playing 10 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps. Despite the low snap counts, the running back influenced many areas of the box score. Etienne continues to be the reserve option behind bell-cow back Chuba Hubbard, who continues to amass carries and touchdowns for the Panthers offense.
injuryReports.injury: Etienne rushed six times for 29 yards, caught one pass for seven yards, logged 36 kick return yards and eight punt return yards in the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuryReports.returnComment: Fitzgerald was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the second straight week and seventh time overall this season. The kicker made a 33-yard field goal in the third quarter before he converted a 37-yarder with 1:44 left in the fourth quarter, ultimately putting the Panthers in front 35-33. Fitzgerald has now gone 17-for-19 on field-goal attempts, including 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, while converting 21 of 26 extra-point tries over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Fitzgerald went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Jaycee Horn
injuryReports.returnComment: Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Jalen Coker
injuryReports.returnComment: Coker endured a helmet-to-helmet hit at the end of a six-yard catch in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win against the Ravens, getting shaken up in the process. Afterward, be reportedly entered the concussion protocol, but one day later he doesn't have a head injury. Coker thus is in the clear ahead of next Monday's game at Tampa Bay.
injuryReports.injury: Hrad coach Dave Canales said Monday that Coker has been cleared from the concussion protocol, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Feleipe Franks
injuryReports.returnComment: Franks has been active for all 10 of the Panthers' games to date, but he's been utilized almost exclusively on special teams. He hasn't logged more than nine snaps on offense in any contest and has yet to draw a target.
injuryReports.injury: Franks played all 21 of his snaps on special teams and was credited with two tackles in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Mitchell Evans
injuryReports.returnComment: Evans was able to reel in a season-high five passes while notching multiple receptions for the fourth time in five weeks. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the first quarter when he secured a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Bryce Young, registering his first score of the year. Evans has now caught 17 of 20 targets for 191 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Evans caught all five of his targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Darren Waller
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end was out-produced by second-year player Mitchell Evans, who posted a 5-44-1 line on five targets, but Waller made more of an impact than Tommy Tremble, who caught his only target for 18 yards. With all three members of the trio capable of making a splash in any given week, Waller will be tough to rely on heading into a Week 12 meeting with the Buccaneers.
injuryReports.injury: Waller caught all three of his targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Young
injuryReports.returnComment: The fourth-year QB posted his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3 percent) while tossing multiple TDs for the third time in the last six contests, a stretch in which he's compiled a 9:5 TD:INT. Both of Young's scores came in the first half, as he connected with Mitchell Evans on a 23-yard TD and Tetairoa McMillan on a seven-yard strike. Young will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against Tampa Bay.
injuryReports.injury: Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-33 win over Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year wideout posted his best yardage total since Week 6 while leading the Panthers in receiving yards, catches and targets. McMillan capped his solid performance with a seven-yard TD from Bryce Young in the second quarter. McMillan has slowed down since a torrid start to the season, but he still sports a 55-731-4 line on 87 targets through 10 games heading into a Week 12 clash with the Buccaneers.
injuryReports.injury: McMillan caught six of nine targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Chuba Hubbard
injuryReports.returnComment: The 27-year-old running back continues to shine, making two trips to the end zone for a second straight week and piling up at least 120 rushing yards for the third time in 2026. Hubbard is handling a bell-cow workload with no issues, and over six games since the Panthers' bye he's averaging nearly 25 touches a game while amassing 688 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns. Jonathon Brooks (groin) seems close to coming off IR, but but he's unlikely to make much of a dent in Hubbard's role as long as the team's top RB is dominating. Hubbard faces a very tough test in Week 12 against a Tampa Bay defense that held him to just 60 combined yards and zero TDs in their first meeting in Week 7.
injuryReports.injury: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 120 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens. He added a two-point conversion.

injuryReports.name: Mike Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and has practiced in full since then. He was listed as questionable to suit up versus Baltimore, though he is now cleared to play for the first time since Week 3.
injuryReports.injury: Jackson (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders has appeared in just one game this season, which was in Week 9 versus Denver. With Darren Waller (knee) and Tommy Tremble (knee) both active, Sanders will now miss his second consecutive contest. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 versus Tampa Bay.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Baltimore, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Haynes King
injuryReports.returnComment: King will only play Sunday if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Ravens on Sunday, Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.

injuryReports.name: Brady Christensen
injuryReports.returnComment: The offensive lineman had his 21-day practice window opened 18 days ago, so a decision will need to be made one way or another on activating him from injured reserve next week. Christensen hasn't played in a game this season.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Simmons
injuryReports.returnComment: Simmons will be required to miss at least the next four games for Carolina. He's logged just six defensive snaps this season and another 206 on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jonathon Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks was a full practice participant in all three sessions during Week 11 prep. However, the third-year running back is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, and he's slated to miss his eighth consecutive game while recovering from a groin injury. Trevor Etienne, Anthony Tyus and AJ Dillon will continue to operate as the Panthers' backfield depth options behind Chuba Hubbard in the absence of Brooks, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Kyler Gordon
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Cam Lewis
injuryReports.returnComment: Playing in his 85th career regular-season games, Lewis' first-quarter sack of Tyler Shough on third-and-11 was the first of the safety's career. Lewis has started eight of the nine games in which he's appeared this season, logging 42 tackles (30 solo) and two pass breakups, including an interception.
injuryReports.injury: Lewis recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Dillon Thieneman
injuryReports.returnComment: Thieneman picked off Tyler Shough in New Orleans' territory in the second quarter, and the Bears turned it into a touchdown three plays later to go up 16-0. It was Thieneman's second interception of the season. The rookie safety is up to 64 tackles (34 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and six pass breakups across 10 games.
injuryReports.injury: Thiemenan recorded seven tackles (three solo) and an interception in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Jeffery Simmons
injuryReports.returnComment: Picked up from the Titans ahead of the trade deadline, Simmons has been everything the Bears could've imagined and then some in three games with his new team. He's up to 14 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and a pair of pass breakups since joining Chicago.
injuryReports.injury: Simmons recorded four tackles (three solo), including 3.0 sacks, in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Sam Roush
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie third-rounder connected with Caleb Williams on a 19-yard pass midway through the first quarter, although Roush didn't see another target the rest of the way. With Cole Kmet (knee, IR) out for the rest of the year, Roush will continue to serve as the Bears' TE2 behind Colston Loveland. The Bears will be on the road for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks dead last in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.
injuryReports.injury: Roush brought in his lone target for 19 yards during Chicago's 21-13 win over New Orleans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Roschon Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: The running back injured his ankle on kickoff coverage in the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Saints and had to be carted off. He'll have two more chances to get on the practice field ahead of Thursday's matchup with the Lions, but he does not appear likely to play at this point. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai are healthy at the top of Chicago's running back depth chart.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Zavion Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams on passes for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be something that the Bears lean into for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (233.1) and 29th in passing touchdowns allowed (21).
injuryReports.injury: Thomas brought in two of three targets for 56 yards and added a 30-yard carry during the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Theo Benedet
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Kalif Raymond
injuryReports.returnComment: Raymond's four targets were tied with Rome Odunze for most on the Bears on Sunday, although the former could only muster a 14-yard grab early in the second quarter. Raymond has commanded four targets or more in six of 10 regular-season games and is up to a 33-304-1 receiving line on 45 targets while operating as Chicago's WR3 behind Odunze and Luther Burden. The Bears will hit the road to face the Lions on Thanksgiving Day.
injuryReports.injury: Raymond caught one of four passes for 14 yards during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Salvon Ahmed
injuryReports.returnComment: The running back was elevated from the practice squad Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against New Orleans, and he carried the ball six times for 33 yards across 10 offensive snaps. Ahmed saw action late in the third quarter and into the fourth, after Roschon Johnson exited the game with an ankle injury in the first quarter. Both are behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai on the depth chart.
injuryReports.injury: Ahmed reverted to the Bears' practice squad Monday, according to the NFL's official transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Cairo Santos
injuryReports.returnComment: Santos got the Bears on the board with a 41-yard field goal in the fourth quarter before connecting on a 35-yarder in the third. His second point-after try in the second quarter missed to the right, and it was the first missed PAT of the 2026 season for the veteran kicker. Santos' 29 extra points are tied for sixth-most in the NFL, and he's 17-for-21 on field-goal attempts (including 3-for-5 on tries from 50-plus yards) through 10 regular-season games. Operating on a short week, the Bears will hit the road for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Santos made both of his field-goal attempts and went 1-for-2 on extra-point tries during the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Stephen Carlson
injuryReports.returnComment: Though he's been active for each of the Bears' last three games in the wake of Cole Kmet's season-ending knee injury, Carlson remains well behind Colston Loveland and Sam Roush in the pecking order at tight end. Carlson has yet to draw a target and has now played more snaps on special teams than offense in the past two contests.
injuryReports.injury: Carlson played 15 of his 19 snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Colston Loveland
injuryReports.returnComment: While he didn't get much target volume, Loveland was still able to make an impact with a 15-yard TD reception in the second quarter that saw him hurdle a defender without even breaking stride on his way to the end zone. It was the tight end's third score of the season, all of which have come during Chicago's current five-game win streak, and after a slow start to the season Loveland has delivered a 27-282-3 line on 37 targets during that period. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 12 against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Loveland caught all three of his targets for 29 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Rome Odunze
injuryReports.returnComment: The four grabs led the Bears on the afternoon, as the offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye. Odunze's longest gain went for just 19 yards, and rookie Zavion Thomas wound up leading the team in receiving yards thanks to a 40-yard connection with Caleb Williams in the third quarter. Odunze has caught exactly four passes in four straight games, a stretch in which he's produced a 16-261-1 line on 22 targets. The third-year wideout will try to get more involved in a potential Week 12 barn burner against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Odunze caught all four of his targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Luther Burden III
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the worst performance of the season for Burden, who suffered a concussion in the Bears' last game in Week 9 but used a bye week to clear the protocol and avoid missing any additional time. The second-year wideout saw his three-game scoring streak come to an end, and on the season he sports a 51-654-4 line on 69 targets through 10 contests. Burden will look to bounce back in a potential Week 12 barn burner against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Burden caught two of three targets for 10 yards and added three yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 win over New Orleans.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bears' offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye, and both of Williams' TD passes came in the second quarter as he connected with D'Andre Swift on a three-yard shovel pass and Colston Loveland on a 15-yard score. Williams failed to reach 200 passing yards for the first time since Week 2, and he'll take a somewhat disappointing 10:6 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 12 clash with the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Williams completed 15 of 23 passes for 181 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints. He added 11 rushing yards on four carries.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Monangai
injuryReports.returnComment: Making his return from a five-game absence due to turf toe, Monangai wasn't able to generate much offense, as D'Andre Swift led the backfield with 15 touches and 59 scrimmage yards, plus a short receiving TD. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Monangai should see his usage increase as he puts the injury further behind him, and a late lost fumble by Swift -- his third of the season, a new career high -- might encourage coach Ben Johnson to prioritize Monangai even more in Week 12 against the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Monangai carried the ball eight times for 18 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: D'Andre Swift
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bears' offense looked a little sluggish coming out of its bye, and Swift wound up leading the backfield in scrimmage yards on the afternoon, highlighting his performance with a three-yard TD pass from Caleb Williams in the second quarter. Swift's 15 touches also led the backfield, as a returning Kyle Monangai got eased back into action with eight touches. Surprisingly, Salvon Ahmed also handled six carries, all in the fourth quarter when the game seemed well in hand. Swift did lose his third fumble of the season, a new career high, but the TD was his 11th of the year, also a new personal best. Monangai could see his workload increase as he puts his turf toe injury further behind him, but Swift seems to have a firm hold of the No. 1 job heading into a Week 12 clash with the team that drafted him in 2020, the Lions.
injuryReports.injury: Swift carried the ball 13 times for 51 yards and caught both his targets for eight yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Case Keenum
injuryReports.returnComment: It's the fifth straight week that Keenum will work as the Bears' emergency third quarterback. That means he can enter Sunday's contest only if both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as Chicago's emergency third quarterback Sunday versus the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Tyrique Stevenson Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevenson injured his hand during the Bears' Week 9 win over the Buccaneers. He had additional time to rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and given Stevenson's absence from Wednesday's estimated practice report, the fourth-year defensive back should suit up Sunday against the Saints. He has accumulated 34 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Stevenson (hand) was not listed on the Bears' estimated injury report Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Jaylon Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: In a game that featured seven turnovers between the two teams, Johnson's takeaway was arguably the most impactful of them all. He jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Cade Otton late in the third quarter, which Johnson returned 67 yards to the house for the second pick-six of his NFL career. The veteran defensive back is up to 27 tackles (21 solo), three pass defenses (including a pick-six) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson recorded three tackles (one solo) and a pick-six during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Risner
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end finished with a team-high yardage total while coming just a yard short of equaling his best tally of the season as well. Gesicki's biggest catch came late in the fourth quarter on the Bengals' final drive, when he hauled in a 32-yard pass from Joe Burrow over the middle to get the Bengals down to  the Commanders' 33-yard line. Gesicki's production continues to have some game-to-game volatility, but he'll draw another favorable matchup in a Week 12 home clash with the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki brought in five of six targets for 77 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Chase Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: As his final line indicates, Brown was completely stonewalled by a talented Commanders run defense, although backfield mate Samaje Perine, who equaled Brown's carry total, was able to average 4.3 yards per tote with his opportunities and  added 71 receiving yards. Brown did find a way to make his usual impact as a receiver, tying for the team lead in receptions and finishing second in targets to Ja'Marr Chase. Brown's carry and rushing yardage totals were both season lows, but he should have appreciably better conditions for production on the ground in a Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Brown rushed six times for six yards and brought in five of eight targets for 30 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: Although Joe Burrow threw for 300 yards, both Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase found tough sledding against a Commanders secondary geared up to stop them. Higgins did salvage his fantasy night with his seventh touchdown catch of the season on a picturesque over-the-shoulder 31-yard grab down the left sideline on the first play after the two-minute warning in the first half. Higgins has six of his scoring receptions in the last five games heading into a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins brought in two of three targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuryReports.returnComment: The Commanders focused on keeping Chase in check after his 231-yard outburst against the Steelers in Week 10, and they executed that plan to near perfection. The superstar wideout finished with his third-lowest yardage total of the season, and his sparsest since Week 4. Chase still extended his streak of five-plus-catch efforts to six games, and he'll look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 12 home matchup against a vulnerable Saints defense Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Chase secured five of nine targets for 31 yards in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bengals' offense started slowly and was shut out altogether in the first quarter, but Burrow was able to lead his team to 10 second-quarter points partly via a 31-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. The prolific signal-caller added a four-yard scoring toss to Colbie Young in the third quarter, and Burrow then helped lead Cincinnati downfield for a go-ahead Evan McPherson 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining, albeit after narrowly avoiding an interception and then taking a third-down sack. Nevertheless, the Bengals came up short when Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a five-play, 64-yard game-winning march, but Burrow finished with his fourth tally of at least 300 passing yards this season. He'll look to put his team back in the win column in a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Burrow completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Bryan Cook
injuryReports.returnComment: The safety suffered a right ankle injury late in the first half and was questionable to return. Now that he's back, he should be able to resume his role in the lineup at free safety.
injuryReports.injury: Cook (ankle) has returned to Monday night's matchup with the Commanders, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Brian Parker II
injuryReports.returnComment: Parker has returned to the active roster after being placed on IR in late August with an undisclosed injury. The rookie sixth-round pick is set to suit up for his first regular-season contest as a reserve offensive lineman.
injuryReports.injury: Parker (undisclosed) is active for Monday night's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Swayze Bozeman
injuryReports.returnComment: The Bengals designated Bozeman to return from injured reserve Nov. 19. The linebacker is set to suit up for his first game since he suffered a broken forearm in Week 5 against the Dolphins, and he'll serve as the primary reserve option at linebacker behind Demetrius Knight and Jack Kiser.
injuryReports.injury: Bozeman (forearm) is active for Monday night's game against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger drew the questionable tag for Monday Night Football, but the veteran safety will end up missing a fourth consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury. He logged full practices during Week 11 prep, so there's a chance he makes his return in Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Dax Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill was absent from practice for the entire week due to an illness, but he is now good to go for Monday Night Football. The 26-year-old will operate in his starting role at slot cornerback versus Washington.
injuryReports.injury: Hill (illness) is active for Monday night's contest against the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Iosivas will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week, after the Bengals had listed him as doubtful heading into Monday's contest following a trio of full practices from Thursday through Saturday. If the fourth-year wideout can turn in another full slate of practices in Week 12, he should have a better chance of being restored to the 53-man roster ahead of the Bengals' Nov. 29 matchup with the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Oren Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Joe Flacco
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.
injuryReports.injury: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Battle
injuryReports.returnComment: Battle ranked second on Cincinnati in stops. One of his six tackles went for a loss, and the 25-year-old also forced a fumble, though it was recovered by the Steelers. Battle has played every defensive snap in seven of the Bengals' nine contests this season, and he's collected 58 tackles and eight defensed passes, including three interceptions.
injuryReports.injury: Battle finished Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh with six tackles (four solo), one defensed pass and one forced fumble.

injuryReports.name: Demetrius Knight Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight led Cincinnati in tackles in the blowout win. The second-year linebacker has recorded exactly eight stops in four of his past five games, and he's finished with at least that tally in all but three of his appearances overall this season. Knight hasn't yet recorded a sack, but he's on pace to blow by his rookie total of 106 stops, as he has 71 tackles across nine games.
injuryReports.injury: Knight finished with eight tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass against the Steelers in a 38-18 victory Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Barrett Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter's tackle tally tied for second-most on the Bengals. The second-year pro has now reached the six-tackle mark in all but one of his nine games this season. Carter leads the Bengals with 74 stops overall, and he's recorded 1.5 sacks, five defensed passes (including an interception) and two forced fumbles.
injuryReports.injury: Carter posted six tackles (two solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Drew Sample
injuryReports.returnComment: Sample entered the contest with no catches over his previous two games, but he tied season-high marks in both receptions and targets versus the Steelers. He gave Cincinnati a two-score lead just after the beginning of the second quarter when he hauled in a three-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Sample has two touchdowns over his past four games, but with just five catches for 39 yards during that span, he's almost entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to generate useful fantasy production.
injuryReports.injury: Sample caught all three of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-18 win against Pittsburgh.

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: McPherson converted a 24-yard field-goal attempt on the first drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to miss a 43-yarder in the second quarter of the contest, though the miss did not end up mattering to the final result of the game. McPherson is now 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts and 33-for-33 on PATs over nine contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McPherson made one of his two field-goal attempts and all five PATs in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Ronnie Hickman
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Tyson Campbell
injuryReports.returnComment: Campbell's three defended passes matched his season total heading into the contest. The cornerback's biggest moment of the day was intercepting C.J. Stroud at the Cleveland 24-yard line with 48 seconds left in the first half. Campbell's turnover likely stole at least three points from the Texans in a game that was decided by the same swing.
injuryReports.injury: Campbell logged five tackles (one solo) and three passes defensed, including one interception, in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Carson Schwesinger
injuryReports.returnComment: Schwesinger continues to be a model of consistency, having played all 658 defensive snaps for the Browns in 2026. The middle linebacker has logged double-digit tackles in six of the team's 10 contests so far, adding 3.0 sacks and three forced fumbles over that span.
injuryReports.injury: Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (eight solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Corley
injuryReports.returnComment: Corley had not caught a pass across the first nine games of the campaign before hauling in three passes during Sunday's victory. He ended up finishing the contest third on the team in receiving yards behind Harold Fannin and Jerry Jeudy.
injuryReports.injury: Corley caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in addition to returning two kicks for 51 yards during Cleveland's win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tylan Wallace
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallace again played a rotational role in Week 10, logging 13 snaps at wide receiver. He was able to draw a season-high two targets and come down with both of them, making him one of eight Browns to catch a pass from quarterback Deshaun Watson Sunday. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on the depth chart, he doesn't have a clear path to more consistent playing time following Cleveland's bye in Week 11.
injuryReports.injury: Wallace caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Texans. He also recorded one tackle in kick coverage.

injuryReports.name: Andre Szmyt
