injuryReports.returnComment: Szmyt knocked through field goals from 49 and 26 yards in Sunday's contest. The kicker stumbled in the fourth quarter, missing a 54-yard attempt with 11:02 remaining that would've brought the game within a point. Szmyt is now 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 15-for-16 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Szmyt made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three of his PATs in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
injuryReports.returnComment: Since Week 7, McLaughlin has logged just three snaps on offense in the Browns' ensuing three games, but prior to Sunday, he still appeared to be in the mix for work on kickoff returns. However, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley have since taken over as the team's preferred kickoff returners, leaving McLaughlin without a role on special teams. McLaughlin will likely continue to see little use as Cleveland's No. 3 back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.
injuryReports.injury: McLaughlin was limited to one snap on offense and none on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Sampson
injuryReports.returnComment: Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79  yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.
injuryReports.injury: Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Jerry Jeudy
injuryReports.returnComment: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.
injuryReports.injury: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: KC Concepcion
injuryReports.returnComment: Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.
injuryReports.injury: Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry.

injuryReports.name: Denzel Boston
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.
injuryReports.injury: Boston caught just one pass for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Deshaun Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 49 yards and a score in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Cleveland.

injuryReports.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Fannin led the Browns across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 30-yard grab on Cleveland's penultimate possession set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning five-yard touchdown rush on the next play. Fannin's chemistry with Deshaun Watson has been outstanding, and the second-year tight end now has at least 91 receiving yards in three of the past four games. Fannin will remain a central figure in Cleveland's impressive air attack when the team returns to action in a home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.
injuryReports.injury: Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 91 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Quinshon Judkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Judkins' rushing volume was at a season-low level, but the second-year back managed to record his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a five-yard run with just under a minute remaining. That proved to be the game-winning score, and Judkins also mustered his second-highest receiving yardage tally of the campaign. The 2025 first-round pick is averaging just 3.4 yards per carry, however, so he remains far from efficient heading into a Week 11 bye ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of five targets for 33 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Derek Barnett
injuryReports.returnComment: Barnett left in the first quarter due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran defensive lineman was cleared by medical staff to return to Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Barnett (hamstring) has returned to Sunday's game against Houston, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

injuryReports.name: Michael Burton
injuryReports.returnComment: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Quincy Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams has had his practice reps over the last couple of weeks limited while tending to a hamstring injury, but he has yet to miss a regular-season game, and that trend will continue for Sunday's home tilt. The veteran linebacker has accumulated 62 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and four forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Williams (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Houston.

injuryReports.name: Denzel Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: Ward was managing a quad injury during all of Week 10 prep, but he avoided an injury tag for Sunday's game despite not logging a full practice. The veteran defensive back has 34 tackles (19 solo), nine pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Ward (quadriceps) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans.

injuryReports.name: P.J. Locke
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Mingo
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jaishawn Barham
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Caleb Downs
injuryReports.returnComment: The No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Downs has started all 11 games this season and has piled up 73 tackles (40 solo), including 2.0 sacks, three pass breakups, including an interception, and two forced fumbles on 92 percent of the Cowboys' defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Downs recorded seven tackles (five solo) in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Shemar James
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year linebacker has started each of the last five games for Dallas and has played at least 88 percent of the defensive snaps in all five. Especially with Dee Winters (knee) injured against Tennessee, James should remain in the starting lineup Thursday against the Eagles. James has 44 tackles (28 solo), one interception and a fumble recovery across 11 contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: James recorded six tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: James Houston
injuryReports.returnComment: The fifth-year edge rusher entered Sunday with 1.5 sacks on the season, so he more than doubled that number with his big game. With Malachi Lawrence (ankle) on injured reserve, Houston's snaps have been dialed up over the last three games. Through seven contests this season, Houston has 18 tackles (nine solo), including 3.5 sacks, and six QB hits.
injuryReports.injury: Houston recorded four tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Quinnen Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The star defensive tackle has been one the select few bright spots on the Dallas defense this season. He leads the league with 18 tackles for loss through 11 games and has racked up 51 total tackles (30 solo), including 8.0 sacks, four forced fumbles and two pass breakups on 65 percent of the defensive snaps. Williams could be looking at another All-Pro selection in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Williams recorded five tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, one forced fumble and a pass breakup in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Luke Schoonmaker
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jake Ferguson (knee) remaining out for Dallas, Schoonmaker played 25 of 65 offensive snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford. Schoonmaker ran 12 routes, five fewer than Spann-Ford, and the duo combined to see three targets on a day Dak Prescott attempted 33 passes. Schoonmaker has five catches for 48 yards on six targets across nine games this season and has no fantasy appeal.
injuryReports.injury: Schoonmaker caught his lone target for six yards in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jake Ferguson (knee) still sidelined, Spann-Ford played 44 of 65 offensive snaps against Tennessee and ran 17 routes on Day Prescott's 36 dropbacks. The Cowboys don't throw to their tight ends often and funnel most targets through CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but Spann-Ford did catch a two-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter. He has 18 catches for 161 yards and the one score on 26 targets across 11 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Spann-Ford caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Jashaun Corbin
injuryReports.returnComment: Corbin was elevated to the active roster for the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday. He finished that contest with five carries for 32 yards and one catch (on as many targets) for five yards, and those touches were spread across four quarters while he operated Javonte Williams' backup. With Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) both on injured reserve, Corbin is a top candidate to be elevated for Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
injuryReports.injury: Corbin reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Dee Winters
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran linebacker was injured in Sunday's win over the Titans and was unable to return to the contest. Now on a short week ahead of Thursday's game against the Eagles, Winters will be up against the clock to get ready for the Thanksgiving contest. DeMarvion Overshown would likely draw the start in Winters' place if the latter is unable to play.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jake Ferguson
injuryReports.returnComment: While Ferguson was present for Monday's walkthrough, per Todd Archer of ESPN.com, he'll officially log a 'DNP' listing for the session as the Cowboys prepare for Thursday afternoon's game against the Eagles. Ferguson, who has missed two straight contests, was deemed a non-participant on practice reports over the past two weeks, with Monday's 'DNP' now giving the tight end two more chances to upgrade his listed participation level ahead of Week 12 action.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: DaRon Bland
injuryReports.returnComment: Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending. The earliest Bland will be eligible to make his return is the Week 16 matchup versus Jacksonville, and Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant should continue to see increased playing time in his absence.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: James Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: The fifth-year tight end was one of eight pass catchers that quarterback Dak Prescott connected with on the afternoon, with the pair of receptions marking Mitchell's first two grabs of the season. Mitchell took the field for 15 of the Cowboys' 65 snaps on offense, but he could wind up seeing most of his playing time on special teams once top tight end Jake Ferguson is cleared to return from the knee injury that has sidelined him for the past two games.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell recorded two receptions for 40 yards on two targets in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Booker
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cowboys scored touchdowns on each of their first six possessions against Tennessee, so Aubrey was busy kicking extra points. His field goal was good from 49 yards in the second half. It's been a struggle at times for Aubrey this season, as he's made just 20 of 25 field-goal tries through 11 games, but he's 31-for-33 on extra points in Dallas' high-octane offense.
injuryReports.injury: Aubrey made his lone field-goal attempt and all six PATs in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Flournoy
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cowboys' slot receiver drew just one look on Dak Prescott's 33 pass attempts. He'd caught multiple passes in all 10 games leading up to Sunday's contest. A favorite target of Prescott in the red zone, Flournoy will try to rebound at home against the Eagles on Thanksgiving, when he'll be playable on three-game fantasy slates for Thursday.
injuryReports.injury: Flournoy caught just one pass for 11 yards on one target in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: KaVontae Turpin
injuryReports.returnComment: Turpin went without a catch for the fourth time this season, but he was able to make his mark as a rusher in Week 11. The wideout was able to break loose for a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, notching his second score on the ground this season. Turpin has now caught five of 11 targets for 49 yards, rushed five times for 60 yards and two touchdowns, and added 695 kick-return yards and 121 yards as a punt returner over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.
injuryReports.injury: Turpin failed to reel in his only target while rushing twice for 41 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans. He added 121 yards as a kick returner and logged a 13-yard punt return.

injuryReports.name: Javonte Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams continued his highly fantasy-friendly season with his third multi-touchdown showing of the season. The veteran back first struck from one yard out to cap off the opening possession of the game, and he added his second scoring grab of 2026 on an 11-yard catch early in the third quarter. Williams has over 60 rushing yards in three straight games, and he's up to 10 rush TDs, his second double-digit tally in as many seasons, heading into Thursday's home divisional Thanksgiving clash with the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Williams rushed 18 times for 67 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 24 yards and another score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: George Pickens
injuryReports.returnComment: Pickens played second fiddle to CeeDee Lamb (11-132-1) in Sunday's blowout win, but that still equated to a rewarding effort for the franchise-tagged receiver. The game marked Pickens' third 100-yard tally of the season and second straight, and he now has seen double-digit targets in four of the last six games overall. Pickens rounded out his day Sunday with his sixth touchdown reception of the campaign on a 10-yard catch in the latter portion of the second quarter, and he should be teed up for another busy day when the Cowboys host the Eagles for a Week 12 matchup on Thanksgiving Day.
injuryReports.injury: Pickens secured seven of 10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: CeeDee Lamb
injuryReports.returnComment: Lamb's near-perfect day included his fifth 100-yard effort of the season -- including his second in the last three games -- and his ninth touchdown grab, which came from eight yards out early in the second quarter. Lamb had six double-digit-yardage catches overall on the afternoon, including his game-long 29-yard grab in the first half. Lamb crossed the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth consecutive season in the process, and he'll take an 88-1,108-9 line into a Week 12 Thanksgiving Day clash at home against the Eagles.
injuryReports.injury: Lamb brought 11 of 12 targets for 132 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dak Prescott
injuryReports.returnComment: As the final score and Prescott's numbers indicate, the prolific passer was clicking on all cylinders right out of the gate against an overmatched Titans defense. Prescott had already helped stake the Cowboys to a 27-6 lead by halftime with eight- and 10-yard touchdown strikes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, respectively. Prescott struck again through the air in the second half with an 11-yard touchdown pass to Javonte Williams before closing out his touchdown tally with a two-yard toss to Brevyn Spann-Ford with just under five minutes remaining. Prescott added his second rushing touchdown of the campaign on a two-yard run in the latter portion of the third quarter, giving him his second straight five-TD performance. Prescott is up to 3,049 passing yards and a 25:6 TD:INT heading into a Thanksgiving Day home clash with the Eagles in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and added four carries for nine yards and another score in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: Thompson was a full participant in practice both Thursday and Friday, but the veteran safety is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve. He'll end up missing an eighth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury he picked up in Week 3 against the Ravens. Thompson's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Donovan Ezeiruaku
injuryReports.returnComment: Ezeiruaku didn't play against the 49ers in Week 10 due to an ankle injury. He's avoided an injury tag for Week 11 after logging a full practice Friday, and his return means less rotational snaps at the edge rusher position will be available for James Houston and Von Miller. Ezeiruaku has 32 tackles (16 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Ezeiruaku (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Alex Singleton
injuryReports.returnComment: Singleton was able to notch double-digit stops for the fourth time in the last five games and sixth time overall this year. The linebacker also notched a sack for the third time in four weeks, getting to Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza for a 10-yard loss in the second quarter. Singleton is now up to 118 total tackles (54 solo), including 3.0 sacks, while also registering three passes defensed over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Singleton recorded 11 total tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed during Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Quan McMillian
injuryReports.returnComment: McMillian had himself a day in Week 11, finishing second on the team in takedowns behind linebacker Alex Singleton (11). The cornerback was also able to strip Raiders running back Mike Washington in the third quarter, but Washington jumped on the loose ball. McMillian's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter though, notching a 35-yard pick-six on an outside pass from quarterback Fernando Mendoza with two minutes left in regulation. McMillian has now registered 39 total tackles (25 solo), including 3.0 sacks, while also adding two interceptions, a forced fumble and a defensive touchdown over 10 contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McMillian recorded eight total tackles (four solo), a forced fumble and a pick-six during Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Troy Franklin
injuryReports.returnComment: The wide receiver did see two targets, but he wasn't able to haul them in. Franklin has just 17 targets across 10 games this year, making nine catches for 100 yards and no scores.
injuryReports.injury: Franklin did not record a catch in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Adam Trautman
injuryReports.returnComment: Trautman leaked open behind Las Vegas' defense on a play-action pass from the goal line early in the second quarter, giving Denver a 10-0 lead. He still has a big role in the Broncos' offense, but he isn't running enough routes to sustain pass-catching production worth fantasy consideration in most formats.
injuryReports.injury: Trautman caught his only target for a one-yard touchdown during Sunday's 38-24 win versus the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Marvin Mims Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Mims reeled in just one pass for the second straight game, but his 36-yard snag in the second quarter was enough to notch his second highest receiving yardage total in a contest this year. The wideout played just 15 snaps on offense, which ranked fifth at his position behind Courtland Sutton (49), Pat Bryant (40), Jaylen Waddle (39) and Troy Franklin (24) for Denver in Week 11. Mims will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of Friday's matchup with the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Mims caught one of two targets for 36 yards and also added an 11-yard rush and 22 yards as a punt returner during Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: J.K. Dobbins
injuryReports.returnComment: Dobbins' opportunities have been dwindling since Week 7 against Arizona, when he dropped to 14 offensive snaps after tallying 31 the week prior. That contest against the Cardinals was when rookie Jonah Coleman returned from a four-game absence, and Coleman has since forced his way into Denver's lead-RB role with blossoming production that has included five rushing TDs over his past three games. Coleman got nearly every running-back snap for Denver on Sunday, with practice-squad elevation Cody Schrader logging just two snaps and Dobbins one. Despite Payton's proclamation that Dobbins still has a "super important" role with the team, there's little reason to expect him to be a reliable fantasy asset as long as Coleman is healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Dobbins logged just one snap in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders, though head coach Sean Payton said Monday that Dobbins "is going to be super important" moving forward, Will Petersen of 104.3 The Fan reports.

injuryReports.name: Wil Lutz
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran kicker has now gone five straight games without missing a kick, as he's 9-for-9 on field goals and 14-for-14 on extra points in that span. With the Denver offense heating up after a slow start to the campaign, Lutz has become useful in fantasy. On the season, he's 17-for-20 on FGAs and has made all 21 of his PATs.
injuryReports.injury: Lutz made his lone field-goal attempt and all five PATs in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Nate Adkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Adkins was on the field for 30 of the Broncos' 73 snaps on offense, with his 41 percent share representing a season-high mark. The fourth-year tight end out of South Carolina has mainly served as a blocking specialist for Denver, having thus far been limited to a 7-47-3 receiving line on nine targets to go with a six-yard carry through 10 appearances on the season.
injuryReports.injury: Adkins recorded a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Pat Bryant
injuryReports.returnComment: The wideout briefly exited the game in the third quarter after he appeared to tweak his previously injured ankle, but Bryant quickly returned and was able to finish out the contest. His four targets were fourth on the team on a day Bo Nix targeted nine different players on 35 pass attempts. The Denver offense spreads the ball around to five different receivers, three tight ends and its running backs most weeks, making it difficult for any of the pass catchers to post big numbers in the box score.
injuryReports.injury: Bryant caught three passes for 32 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Courtland Sutton
injuryReports.returnComment: Sutton thus was blanked in the box score for the first time Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, a span of 39 games (including playoffs). Considering he's surpassed 50 receiving yards just one time in 10 appearances in 2026, he doesn't hold much sway for fantasy purposes, especially in a Broncos offense that often has sputtered this season. Sutton's next chance to turn the tide arrives Friday at Pittsburgh.
injuryReports.injury: Sutton didn't corral either of his two targets during Sunday's 38-24 victory versus the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Evan Engram
injuryReports.returnComment: It was easily Engram's best performance of the season, as he set season highs in targets, catches and yards against Las Vegas. Entering Sunday, Engram had produced just seven grabs for 48 yards total over his previous four games. Engram and the Broncos have a quick turnaround ahead of Friday's date with the Steelers. The tight end will be a low-floor fantasy option for that one.
injuryReports.injury: Engram caught six of eight targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Bo Nix
injuryReports.returnComment: After a hit-or-miss first six appearances of the season, Nix has settled into a four-game stretch in which his passing yards have ranged from 222 to 237 weekly, a span in which he boasts a 6:2 TD:INT and 84 rushing yards and another score. He also displayed some promise with offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle (3-61-0 on six targets) while connecting with TE Adam Trautman for his 12th touchdown pass in 10 contests. Nix will look to keep things rolling Friday at Pittsburgh.
injuryReports.injury: Nix completed 19 of 35 passes for 225 yards, one touchdown and one interception and notched six carries for five yards during Sunday's 38-24 victory against the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Waddle
injuryReports.returnComment: Waddle sustained a concussion in the Broncos' last game in Week 9 at Carolina, but with the benefit of a Week 10 bye, he had enough time to gain clearance from the protocol for head injuries and miss no additional time as a result. With a 24-yard connection with QB Bo Nix on Sunday, Waddle now has recorded exactly one catch of at least that distance in four straight games. Unfortunately for Waddle's fantasy managers, his 61 receiving yards marked his second most of the campaign after a 138-yard outburst in Week 2 against the Jaguars, so he remains an underwhelming asset in most formats.
injuryReports.injury: Waddle secured three of six targets for 61 yards during Sunday's 38-24 win versus the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Jonah Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: Since returning from an IR stint due to a sprained ankle in Week 7, Coleman has increased his touch count in four consecutive contests, taking a stranglehold on the Broncos backfield in the process. As evidence, his 25 touches easily outpaced fellow RB J.K. Dobbins' one, which went for no yards. Coleman, a rookie fourth-round pick, also cracked the 100-yard mark on the ground for the first time in his career. With RJ Harvey (ankle) on injured reserve for at least one more game, Coleman again is set to act as a workhorse in Friday's road matchup with the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman reeled off 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries and hauled in four of five targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 38-24 win against the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Lil'Jordan Humphrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Humphrey will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Steelers on Black Friday, although Humphrey is unlikely to see the field unless a wide receiver ahead of him on the depth chart is not available.
injuryReports.injury: Humphrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Sam Ehlinger
injuryReports.returnComment: As the emergency QB3, Ehlinger is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Broncos' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Taylor Rapp
injuryReports.returnComment: Rapp was cut from the Broncos' active roster in early November before opting to stick around as a member of the team's practice squad. His elevation gives Denver more depth in the secondary in the event that Brandon Jones (hamstring) cannot play against the Raiders on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: The Broncos signed Rapp from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Talanoa Hufanga
injuryReports.returnComment: Hufanga logged three consecutive full practices during Week 11 prep. The strong safety did not let his persistent ankle injury inhibit him during the week, clearing him of any injury designation that may have followed him into Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Hufanga (ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Lohner
injuryReports.returnComment: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Riley Moss
injuryReports.returnComment: Moss was a full participant in Friday's practice. The newly extended Broncos starter has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest. The team's Week 10 bye helped Moss rest and recover from the injury he sustained during the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Moss (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Ennis Rakestraw Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Brian Branch
injuryReports.returnComment: Branch played 98 percent of the Lions' defensive snaps in the contest. The strong safety has now had two passes defensed in consecutive weeks, totaling five in his five regular-season games in 2026. Week 11 marked the first week of 2026 that Branch and free safety Kirby Joseph played alongside each other. The duo looks to cement the Lions' secondary as the team battles for an NFC North crown.
injuryReports.injury: Branch logged six tackles (one solo) and two passes defensed in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Rock Ya-Sin
injuryReports.returnComment: Ya-Sin played 59 defensive snaps in the contest and one snap on special teams. The cornerback played 91 percent of the team's defensive snaps, starting due to the injury to Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder). Ya-Sin remains the primary backup for the Lions' secondary, proving his consistency in Sunday's win.
injuryReports.injury: Ya-Sin logged 10 tackles (nine solo) in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Saylors
injuryReports.returnComment: Saylors didn't record any stats over two snaps on offense while he notched 29 yards on his only kick return of the day in Week 11. The running back will continue to be unintriguing fantasy option while operating as an extreme depth option behind Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit's backfield moving forward.
injuryReports.injury: Saylors recorded 29-yard kick return during Sunday's 31-21 win over Tampa Bay.

injuryReports.name: Isaac TeSlaa
injuryReports.returnComment: TeSlaa went without a reception for the second time in four weeks, and he has now gone six straight games without exceeding 20 receiving yards. The wide receiver played 23 snaps on offense, ranking third at his position behind Amon-Ra St. Brown (46) and Jameson Williams (45). TeSlaa will continue to be an unreliable fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 12 matchup with the Bears on Thursday.
injuryReports.injury: TeSlaa failed to catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Brock Wright
injuryReports.returnComment: One of Wright's two grabs in Week 11 was a 27-yard strike up the seam, easily his longest reception of the season thus far. He was on the field for 43 of the Lions' 58 offensive snaps Sunday, but he spent a substantial majority of those on blocking assignments for tailback Jahmyr Gibbs and company. His role in a Thanksgiving tilt versus the Bears may depend somewhat on the health of running mate Sam Laporta, who was limited during Monday's walkthrough with an ankle issue.
injuryReports.injury: Wright caught both of two targets for 42 yards during Sunday's 31-21 win versus the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: DJ Wonnum
injuryReports.returnComment: Wonnum registered five solo tackles, including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed and a forced fumble during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. The defensive lineman may have picked up a back injury during the contest, and he will have two more chances to return to practice prior to Thursday's matchup with the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: D.J. Reed
injuryReports.returnComment: Reed appears to be on track to return to action Thursday against the Bears after missing three straight games with a hip injury. The cornerback will have two more chances to officially practice ahead of Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Reed (hip) was considered to be a full participant at the Lions' walkthrough practice Monday.

injuryReports.name: Sione Vaki
injuryReports.returnComment: Of the Lions' 58 offensive snaps in Week 11, Vaki played just 13, his lowest count since back in Week 7 versus the Packers (9). Starter Jahmyr Gibbs compiled 100-plus scrimmage yards and multiple scrimmage touchdowns for the fifth time in 10 games Sunday, so should continue to get all the work he can handle in a Thanksgiving matchup versus the Bears, leaving only whatever is left behind to Vaki.
injuryReports.injury: Vaki took one carry for a loss of one yard and caught his only target for seven yards during Sunday's 31-21 win versus the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Chuck Clark
injuryReports.returnComment: Clark was able to play every defensive snap during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers, notching eight total tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a pass defensed. The safety may have picked up a hamstring injury during the game, and he will have two more chances to return to practice before Thursday's matchup with the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Skyler Gill-Howard
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Sam LaPorta
injuryReports.returnComment: With a Thanksgiving matchup on tap against the Bears, the Lions are easing into the week following Sunday's 31-21 win against the Buccaneers, when LaPorta gathered in three of six targets for 62 yards. He's nursing an ankle issue in the wake of that contest, and he may need to be listed as full Tuesday and/or Wednesday in order to avoid a designation ahead of Thursday's game.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jake Bates
injuryReports.returnComment: The kicker missed a 53-yard try on the Lions' opening drive of the game but later came back to make one from 56 yards in the second quarter. Through 10 games this season, Bates is 17-for-19 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 33-for-33 on extra points. Bates led the league in PATs in the 2024 and 2025 seasons and is again on pace to kick 50-plus extra points in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Bates made one of two field-goal attempts and all four PATs in Sunday's 31-21 win over the Bucs.

injuryReports.name: Jameson Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The highlight of Williams' afternoon was a 57-yard touchdown reception early in the third quarter where he got free on a post pattern, and the fifth-year veteran also led the Lions in receiving yards. Williams has at least four receptions in four of the last five games, and Sunday marked his third game with more than 90 receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick is now averaging 17.0 yards per reception heading into Thursday's Week 12 home matchup against the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Williams brought in all four targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jared Goff
injuryReports.returnComment: Goff put together an efficient effort on an afternoon when he recorded completions to eight different targets. The veteran signal-caller hit Amon-Ra St. Brown (14 yards) and Jameson Williams (57 yards) for his pair of touchdown passes, and he has multiple scoring strikes in two straight. Goff boasts a sparkling 20:4 TD:INT heading into a Thanksgiving Day showdown against the Bears at Ford Field on Thursday.
injuryReports.injury: Goff completed 20 of 28 passes for 279 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding five rushes for 12 yards in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: St. Brown set the pace for the Lions in catches while also tying for the team lead in targets, and the sure-handed receiver also recorded his eighth touchdown reception of the season on a 14-yard grab early in the second quarter that opened the scoring for either team. St. Brown's yardage total left plenty to be desired, but he's still up to a 70-792-8 line on 97 targets heading into Thursday's holiday showdown at home against the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: St. Brown brought in five of six targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
injuryReports.returnComment: Gibbs unsurprisingly had his work cut out for him against the Buccaneers' typically stingy run defense, but the Lions had the luxury of continuing to pound Gibbs into the line while protecting a second-half lead. Gibbs eventually broke through for a game-long 26-yard run and cashed in with one- and four-yard touchdown runs in the fourth quarter to help ice the victory. While Gibbs fell just short of his fifth 100-yard effort in the last six games, the 2023 first-round pick is up to 13 rushing touchdowns and is averaging 5.0 yards per carry heading into a Thanksgiving Day home showdown against the Bears.
injuryReports.injury: Gibbs rushed 23 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns and secured four of five targets for 20 yards in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Dorsey
injuryReports.returnComment: Dorsey hurt his wrist early in Sunday's game and was initially deemed questionable to return. The veteran cornerback has since been able to re-enter the game, albeit with a club over the hand that he injured. Dorsey has been working in a rotational role at cornerback, logging a defensive snap share between 32 and 38 percent three straight weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Dorsey (wrist) has re-entered Sunday's matchup against Tampa Bay, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Lacy
injuryReports.returnComment: Lacy was limited in practice all week due to a shoulder injury, but he's been cleared to play in Sunday's home game. He's expected to take on an elevated role at defensive end in the absence of Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the rest of the season due to a torn ACL. Lacy has accumulated 12 tackles (four solo) through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Lacy (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Cade Mays
injuryReports.returnComment: Mays missed the Lions' two prior games due to an ankle injury that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 8. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against Minnesota. Juice Scruggs figures to be the Lions' starting center for as long as Mays is sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Kevin Zeitler
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Triceps

injuryReports.name: Sean Rhyan
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Skyy Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore re-injured his ankle after just three snaps on special teams in the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings. He's been practicing ahead of Wednesday's game against the Rams, but it remains to be seen if Moore will be able to play. His role on offense has mostly evaporated with the return of Savion Williams behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Bo Melton
injuryReports.returnComment: Melton was injured in the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings and has been limited in practice each of the last two days leading up to Wednesday's game against the Rams. The wide receiver has appeared in all 10 games this season, recording five catches for 34 yards on 10 targets across 150 offensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Thigh

injuryReports.name: Brandon Cisse
injuryReports.returnComment: The Packers' rookie cornerback is ready to go for Wednesday's game against the Rams after he exited Week 10 early against the Vikings. Cisse has started all 10 games this season, recording 38 tackles (26 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and nine pass breakups, including an interception, on 83 percent of the defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Cisse (ribs) practiced fully Monday.

injuryReports.name: Travis Glover
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Shoulder

injuryReports.name: Micah Parsons
injuryReports.returnComment: Parsons has yet to turn in a full practice since being designated for return from the PUP list Nov. 4, but the Packers seemingly haven't closed the door on him making his season debut Wednesday versus the Rams. According to Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com, Parsons said that he's still awaiting final clearance for game action from his surgeon, Dr. Neal ElAttrache, whom he's scheduled to meet with in the next day or two. If Parsons gets the green light to play in Week 12, he could have his snap count managed to some extent.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Josh Jacobs
injuryReports.returnComment: Though Jacobs went down as a limited participant on the second injury report in a row after going through individual drills, head coach Matt LaFleur reiterated prior to Monday's session that the running back is unlikely to play Wednesday versus the Rams. Unless Jacobs takes a notable step forward in his activity during Tuesday's practice that leaves the Packers more optimistic that he'll be ready to play in Los Angeles, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd appear poised to lead the Green Bay ground game in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Finger

injuryReports.name: Zaire Franklin
injuryReports.returnComment: Franklin has missed the Packers' last four games due to the shin injury and isn't yet 100 percent healthy coming out of a Week 11 bye. He was listed as a limited participant Monday for a second straight practice and may need to upgrade to full activity Tuesday to avoid taking a designation into Wednesday.
injuryReports.injury: Shin

injuryReports.name: Kaleb Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Josh Jacobs logged his first official practice Sunday since undergoing finger surgery on Nov. 13, going down as a limited participant. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed to Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site earlier in the day that Jacobs is "gonna have to show a lot of progress" the next few days to be available in Week 12. If Jacobs isn't active Wednesday at the Rams, Johnson may be the favorite to lead Green Bay's backfield in carries and rushing yards, as he did in a Week 10 loss to the Vikings, when he took 10 rushes for 42 yards. Meanwhile, fellow RB MarShawn Lloyd had seven touches for 39 yards from scrimmage in that contest, and Chris Brooks logged three touches for three total yards.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson handled the first RB reps during the open portion of Sunday's practice, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah McDuffie
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Luke Musgrave
injuryReports.returnComment: LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Evan Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams played every single defensive snap in Week 10 and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Packers behind Isaiah McDuffie (10). Williams has recorded at least eight stops in three of his last four outings and is up to 84 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, eight pass defenses (including three interceptions) and a fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games. He is well on track to surpass 100 tackles for a second consecutive year.
injuryReports.injury: Williams logged eight tackles (two solo) and a pass defense during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Xavier McKinney
injuryReports.returnComment: McKinney picked off a deep pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, although the Packers' offense failed to turn that takeaway into points before the end of the half. McKinney has three picks over his last two outings and is up to a league-leading six interceptions. The veteran safety is up to 44 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: McKinney registered six tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10.

injuryReports.name: Savion Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: As he's been doing since making his season debut in Week 6, Williams operated as the Packers' third receiver against Minnesota. He logged 20 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on 37 dropbacks. Williams has yet to hit 50 receiving yards in any of his five games this season and has no real fantasy appeal in 12-team fantasy leagues. He's well behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the order for touches and targets.
injuryReports.injury: Williams caught two passes for 27 yards on two targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Chris Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: It was Brooks' first action since Week 4 after spending five games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. With Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive against Minnesota, Brooks led the backfield with 26 offensive snaps in Week 10, but it didn't translate to touches or opportunities to handle the football. With Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd also involved, it's difficult to pinpoint any of these three as reliable fantasy options despite Jacobs' absence.
injuryReports.injury: Brooks rushed two times for one yard and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: J. Michael Sturdivant
injuryReports.returnComment: After Green Bay was shut out in the first half, Sturdivant's first career touchdown came in the third quarter from 32 yards out, and it went down as the Packers' lone touchdown of the afternoon. Sturdivant played just nine offensive snaps as the fourth receiver and would need more than one injury ahead of him on the depth chart to be relevant in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Sturdivant caught two passes for 37 yards and a touchdown on four targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Trey Smack
injuryReports.returnComment: Smack pushed a 53-yard field-goal try wide right in the first quarter before later converting a 40-yard attempt in the final seconds of the third quarter. The rookie has now gone 15-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while making 21 of 24 extra-point attempts over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Smack went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Tyrod Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Down 20 points with four minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and with starting quarterback Jordan Love having already taken eight sacks on the afternoon, the Packers opted to turn to Taylor to direct the offense for their final possession of the day. All three of Taylor's appearances on the season have now come late in blowout wins or losses, and his opportunities are likely to remain limited to garbage-time situations so long as Love is healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Taylor completed one of two pass attempts for three yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: MarShawn Lloyd
injuryReports.returnComment: With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.
injuryReports.injury: Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards.

injuryReports.name: Tucker Kraft
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end's numbers reflected how much time his quarterback had to look downfield, as Jordan Love got sacked eight times in the rout. Kraft has been held to just one catch in back-to-back games, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 37-370-3 line on 56 targets through 10 games, with the Rams as the next opponent on the horizon in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Kraft caught one of four targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Matthew Golden
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.
injuryReports.injury: Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Christian Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Packers' passing game was stifled as the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, giving him little time to find receivers like Watson. The 37 yards were a season low for the fifth-year wideout, while the three grabs tied for his lowest volume of 2026. Watson will take a 52-916-7 line on 79 targets through 10 contests into a Week 11 bye before facing the Rams in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Watson caught three of five targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Love
injuryReports.returnComment: The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.
injuryReports.injury: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

injuryReports.name: Wyatt Teller
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Brevin Jordan
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Danielle Hunter
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Woody Marks
injuryReports.returnComment: After sustaining a concussion in a Nov. 15 loss to the Browns, Marks was unable to clear the five-step protocol on a short week and ended up sitting out this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts. Since then, Marks appears to have progressed on some level through the protocol, though it's not yet clear if he'll be available to practice when the Texans kick off Week 12 prep Wednesday. If Marks ends up getting the green light to play versus the Ravens, he may be part of a timeshare in the backfield or be forced to settle for No. 2 duties behind David Montgomery (groin), who returned from a four-game absence in Week 11 to run for a season-high 107 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: M.J. Stewart
injuryReports.returnComment: With the return of Reed Blankenship to the starting lineup, Stewart was relegated to special teams. The strong safety played 17 snaps but did not appear in the box score.
injuryReports.injury: Stewart played 17 special-teams snaps in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Henry To'oTo'o
injuryReports.returnComment: To'oTo'o played 100 percent of the Texans' defensive snaps for the second straight week. The linebacker was on the field for all 48 plays, logging four solo tackles in the effort.
injuryReports.injury: To'oTo'o accumulated six tackles (four solo) in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Will Anderson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Anderson extended his NFL sacks lead to 11.5 in Thursday's contest. The pass rusher is amassing another strong season to contend for Defensive Player of the Year. Anderson finished 2025 with 12.0 sacks and is set to surpass that personal record this season.
injuryReports.injury: Anderson logged five tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Foster Moreau
injuryReports.returnComment: Moreau's 30 offensive snaps were second among Texans tight ends behind Dalton Schultz's 34, yet it was Marlin Klein who led the position group with four catches (on as many targets) for 24 yards, including a 13-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud late in the third quarter. Moreau is up to a 12-80-3 receiving line on 15 targets through 10 regular-season games and has caught one pass or zero in five of those contests. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal unless Schultz were to miss time.
injuryReports.injury: Moreau brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
injuryReports.returnComment: Fairbairn's only field goal of the night was a 27-yarder with 15 seconds remaining in the first half. The kicker is 20-for-21 on field-goal attempts and 27-for-27 on PATs over 10 regular-season games so far in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Fairbairn made his sole field-goal attempt and all three PATs in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Emari Demercado
injuryReports.returnComment: With Woody Marks (concussion) inactive, Demercado played the complementary role behind lead back David Montgomery, who rushed 26 times for 107 yards in his return from a multi-week groin injury. Demercado was picked up off waivers from Dallas last month.
injuryReports.injury: Demercado rushed five times for 33 yards and caught both of his targets for minus-four yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Kayshon Boutte
injuryReports.returnComment: The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Xavier Hutchinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.
injuryReports.injury: Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Marlin Klein
injuryReports.returnComment: Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Schultz
injuryReports.returnComment: Schultz had a minimal role on a night when C.J. Stroud threw for a modest 194 yards and recorded completions to nine different targets. The veteran tight end now has consecutive one-catch, 11-yard tallies after recording multiple receptions in each of his first eight games of the season, and Schultz's production will remain hard to trust heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Schultz brought in his only target for 11 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tank Dell
injuryReports.returnComment: The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Dell secured three of four targets for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: C.J. Stroud
injuryReports.returnComment: Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and he'll take a sparkling 22:4 TD:INT into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Stroud completed 21 of 26 passes for 194 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed six times for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nico Collins
injuryReports.returnComment: Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: David Montgomery
injuryReports.returnComment: Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Montgomery functioned as the clear lead back with Woody Marks (concussion) unavailable. The former put together the best rushing yardage total of his brief Texans tenure, handling his highest number of carries since Week 4 of his 2023 debut campaign with the Lions. Montgomery also was encouragingly involved in a complementary role in the passing game, and he'll now have some extra time to recover from Thursday's workload ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29. However, if Marks is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of that contest, Montgomery will see his touch count take a hit.
injuryReports.injury: Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards and brought in three of four targets for 17 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Keylan Rutledge
injuryReports.returnComment: The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.
injuryReports.injury: Undisclosed

injuryReports.name: Trent Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown left Thursday's contest after suffering a back injury, but he was able to check back in with the Texans' field goal team in the second quarter. With that said, veteran Braden Smith was still working as Houston's right tackle when the first half of Thursday's game ended.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (back) has returned to Thursday's game versus the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.

injuryReports.name: Sheldon Rankins
injuryReports.returnComment: Rankins sustained an apparent ankle injury during the second quarter of Thursday's contest, and he was able to walk gingerly to the sideline under his own power. In his absence, rookie second-rounder Kayden McDonald figures to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jake Hummel
injuryReports.returnComment: The linebacker suffered the injury in Week 1, returned for Week 10 and then carried a questionable tag into this contest, but he appears ready to play through the injury for the second consecutive game. Hummel logged two tackles (one solo) across 21 special-teams snaps against the Browns last week.
injuryReports.injury: Hummel (groin) is active for Thursday Night Football against the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Bernhard Raimann
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Jerry Tillery
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Jalen Travis
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Charvarius Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Will Mallory
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Sauce Gardner
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: DJ Giddens
injuryReports.returnComment: Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that McGowan "will miss some time" but didn't specify how long the absence may be. For however long McGowan is sidelined, Giddens figures to serve as Jonathan Taylor's backup at running back. Giddens has shown some flashes this season in limited playing time, amassing 48 yards on seven carries (6.9 YPC) and catching his only target for 11 yards over three games.
injuryReports.injury: Giddens will likely move up to the No. 2 RB role for the Colts in the short term, as Seth McGowan is expected to miss time due to a hamstring injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Seth McGowan
injuryReports.returnComment: McGowan went down with the injury while returning a kickoff in the first half of the Week 11 loss. The rookie seventh-round pick had been solidified as the top backup to starting running back Jonathan Taylor, but DJ Giddens now is positioned to serve as Taylor's main understudy for however long McGowan is sidelined. McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Alec Pierce
injuryReports.returnComment: Steichen rebuffed a report Sunday from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, who relayed that the Colts were planning to "exercise great caution" by holding Pierce out for the season as he works his way back from an aggravation of his surgically repaired heel. However, given the 3-8 Colts' place in the standings in addition to their $114 million investment in Pierce, Steichen acknowledged that the 26-year-old wideout still faces an uphill battle to make it back from IR before season's end if he's anything less than 100 percent. According to James Boyd of The Athletic, Steichen said that Pierce currently is "doing plyometrics" and "running" after landing on IR on Sept. 26, but it's unclear how close Pierce may be to practicing.
injuryReports.injury: Heel

injuryReports.name: Drew Ogletree
injuryReports.returnComment: For the third time in four weeks, Ogletree failed to draw a look in the passing game, but he wasn't held off the stat sheet entirely, as he collected a pair of tackles on special teams. Though the fifth-year tight end has been active for all 11 of the Colts' games, he's cobbled together a lowly 4-21-0 receiving line on seven targets.
injuryReports.injury: Ogletree went without a target while playing 24 of the Colts' 50 snaps on offense in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Pharaoh Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: For the second week in a row, Brown ended up seeing more snaps on special teams (11) than offense. Through four games with Indianapolis, Brown has drawn just one target, which he turned into a seven-yard reception during a Week 6 loss to the Titans.
injuryReports.injury: Brown went without a target while playing eight of the Colts' 50 offensive snaps in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Boettcher
injuryReports.returnComment: Boettcher finished Thursday's game tied for the fourth-most tackles on the Colts. The rookie fourth-rounder has started in each of Indianapolis' last three games, which has lined up with the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR). Boettcher is up to 50 tackles (16 solo) through 11 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Boettcher recorded six tackles (three solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Adetomiwa Adebawore
injuryReports.returnComment: Adebawore recorded his fifth sack of the season early in the third quarter, when he took down C.J. Stroud for a seven-yard loss. Adebawore has already set a career-high in sacks through 11 regular-season games and has accumulated 31 tackles (15 solo), one defense and a scoop-and-score in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Adebawore finished Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans with seven tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks.

injuryReports.name: A.J. Haulcy
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie third-rounder recorded the first interception of his career in the first quarter, when a pass from C.J. Stroud intended for Nico Collins bounced off Haulcy's helmet, off the hands of Cam Bynum and into Haulcy's arms. The LSU product is up to 53 tackles (30 solo) and three pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Haulcy logged nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: CJ Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a busy night for the rookie second-rounder, who finished with a career-high in stops while logging double-digit tackles for the third time this season. Allen has 45 total tackles over his last four outings, and most of that extra playing time has come in the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR).
injuryReports.injury: Allen posted 16 tackles (seven solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Quez Watkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Watkins played just five offensive snaps for the Colts in Thursday night's game. Despite playing only 10 percent of the offensive snaps, Watkins totaled the third-highest yardage by Colts pass catchers on the night with his 26-yard grab. The reserve wide receiver could see an expanded role down the stretch as the Colts experiment with starting quarterback Anthony Richardson in what is all but a lost season.
injuryReports.injury: Watkins caught one of his three targets for 26 yards during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Ashton Dulin
injuryReports.returnComment: Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Dulin caught two of his four targets for 30 yards and assisted on two tackles on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Deion Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.
injuryReports.injury: Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Spencer Shrader
injuryReports.returnComment: Shrader opened Thursday's scoring with a 34-yard field goal early in the first quarter. Those ended up being the only three points scored by the Colts, as Shrader missed a 56-yarder later in the quarter, and his 62-yarder in the second quarter was blocked by Logan Hall. It was the second time this season that Shrader has missed two kicks, and the third-year kicker now is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts (including 9-for-12 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 19-for-20 on extra-point tries through 11 regular-season games. His scoring potential figures to be lower for the rest of the season after the Colts waived Daniel Jones on Friday, which paves the way for Anthony Richardson to start under center in Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Anthony Richardson Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Richardson made a cameo in Thursday's 26-3 loss at Houston, taking over for Jones for Indianapolis' final possession, but the former logged just a two-yard carry and two incompletions before the Texans ate up the final 6:50 of the contest. A 2023 first-round pick, Richardson himself hasn't started since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, making just four brief appearances the past two seasons combined, but he'll have a chance to boost his value (or not) in the final year of his rookie contract.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Shane Steichen announced Friday that Richardson will be the Colts' starting quarterback moving forward after the team waived Daniel Jones.

injuryReports.name: Laquon Treadwell
injuryReports.returnComment: Treadwell played a position-high 40 of 50 offensive snaps but continues to run wind sprints in an offense that doesn't throw the ball down the field. Through 11 games this season, Treadwell has just 19 catches for 239 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets.
injuryReports.injury: Treadwell failed to catch his lone target in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans.

injuryReports.name: Anthony Gould
injuryReports.returnComment: Gould was the rather unlikely leader in receiving yards for the Colts on the night, with a team-high 31-yard catch playing a big role in getting him there. The 2024 fifth-round pick has seen an expanded role in the wake of the trades of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and for as long as Alec Pierce (IR, heel) is sidelined, Gould could function as one of Indianapolis' top downfield threats for either Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard.
injuryReports.injury: Gould secured two of three targets for 48 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Warren
injuryReports.returnComment: The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick now has recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Jones, who James Boyd of The Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after the game, is replaced by Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard under center.
injuryReports.injury: Warren brought in one of five targets for 22 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Taylor put some distance between himself and promising rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan in terms of workload, as the former outpaced his teammate in carries by an 11-3 margin, even with the latter exiting before halftime with a hamstring injury. However, the extra opportunity was a moot point, as Taylor couldn't find any space to operate as either a runner or receiver. Daniel Jones' mediocre play under center certainly isn't helping the ground attack's cause, and Taylor now has recorded less than 50 rushing yards in three of the last four contests. The star running back will have some additional time to prepare for a relatively favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Taylor rushed 11 times for 21 yards and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Danny Striggow
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Matt Dickerson
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Robert Hainsey
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Foyesade Oluokun
injuryReports.returnComment: Oluokun had a solid outing despite the loss, logging a team-high nine tackles while playing every defensive snap. The 2018 sixth-round pick has now totaled 77 tackles (48 solo), including 2.0 sacks, two interceptions and a forced fumble across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Oluokun compiled nine tackles (seven solo) during Jacksonville's loss to the Giants on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: LeQuint Allen Jr.
