injuryReports.name: Ernest Jones IV
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones helped make first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza's NFL debut miserable. The inside linebacker helped the Seahawks' defense contain the young quarterback's scrambling ability while also limiting his mid-range opportunities from the pocket en route to yet another defensive win for the defending champs.
injuryReports.injury: Jones logged 10 tackles (five solo) in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jason Myers
injuryReports.returnComment: Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Myers missed his sole field-goal attempt and made three PATs in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Cooper Kupp
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tory Horton
injuryReports.returnComment: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.
injuryReports.injury: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: AJ Barner
injuryReports.returnComment: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.
injuryReports.injury: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Rashid Shaheed
injuryReports.returnComment: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.
injuryReports.injury: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.

injuryReports.name: Drew Lock
injuryReports.returnComment: Lock took advantage of having WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba at his disposal, targeting him 10 times, one of which resulted in a 71-yard TD connection. Moreover, Lock also hooked up with Cooper Kupp on a sliding 34-yard touchdown, marking his second multi-TD outing in four appearances (three starts) this season. There's an expectation that Seahawks No. 1 QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps) returns from a two-game absence after the team's Week 11 bye, but until he receives a clean bill of health, Lock has a chance to be under center on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and logged six carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory in Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Jadarian Price
injuryReports.returnComment: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Zach Charbonnet
injuryReports.returnComment: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith-Njigba's Week 10 performance was fueled by a 71-yard catch and run for a touchdown in the middle of the third quarter, but he still was able to put up 100 yards on his other seven receptions en route to a new season high in the category. As the Seahawks hit their Week 11 bye, he's reached the century mark in receiving eight times and resides on a 79-1,207-10 line on 109 targets through 10 contests. Smith-Njigba's next chance to continue aggravating opposing defenses arrives Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Smith-Njigba gathered in eight of 10 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 21-13 win at Las Vegas.

injuryReports.name: Jarran Reed
injuryReports.returnComment: Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Abraham Lucas
injuryReports.returnComment: Lucas exited the first quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. The right tackle appears to have sustained a significant injury and likely will not return to the contest. Josh Jones should finish the game at right tackle for the Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Emanuel Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to the lineup in Week 8 against the Bears, Wilson was contained to special teams in that contest and then was active but didn't log a snap last Sunday versus the Cardinals. Now, Wilson will yield all the RB reps to Charbonnet, Price and George Holani in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game at Arizona.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Pili
injuryReports.returnComment: Pili missed the Seahawks' last two games while nursing a back injury, but he's been cleared to play in Week 10 after logging a full practice session Friday. His return gives the Seahawks more depth on the interior defensive line behind Byron Murphy.
injuryReports.injury: Pili (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Uchenna Nwosu
injuryReports.returnComment: Nwosu has missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to an ankle injury, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after ending Week 10 prep with a full practice Friday. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Derick Hall, Dante Fowler and Connor O'Toole.
injuryReports.injury: Nwosu (ankle) does not have an injury designation against the Raiders on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Derick Hall
injuryReports.returnComment: Hall was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 10 prep before sitting out Friday's session. However, his reduced practice reps appear to have been planned by the Seahawks to manage his back injury, and the fourth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. Hall has 24 tackles (14 solo), including 3.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Hall (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Antoine Winfield Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: questionable
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Tez Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: After being benched in the Bucs' pre-Week 9 bye loss to the Bears, ted Hurst was back in the good graces of the coaching staff and played ahead of Johnson as the WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin. That left Johnson as the fourth receiver, playing just 20 of 69 offensive snaps. He has 13 catches for 271 yards and one touchdown on 23 targets across 10 games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson caught two of three targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Simmons
injuryReports.returnComment: Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Benjamin Morrison
injuryReports.returnComment: Both Morrison and Jacob Parrish (back) were injured in Sunday's loss to Detroit, forcing Tampa Bay to dip into its cornerback depth. Kevin Knowles picked up the extra snaps opposing Zyon McCollum, with Keionte Scott covering the slot.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Chase McLaughlin
injuryReports.returnComment: After making multiple field goals in four straight games leading up to Sunday's game, McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal for just the second time this season. The veteran kicker remains perfect on 43 kicks this season, going 22-for-22 on field goals and 21-for-21 on PATs. He's a valuable fantasy kicker headed into next Monday night's home date with the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: McLaughlin made all three of his extra-point attempts in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Jacob Parrish
injuryReports.returnComment: Parrish exited Sunday's Week 11 game against the Lions after sustaining a back injury. The 22-year-old has played in nine games in 2026, recording 40 tackles (33 solo) and 14 pass deflections, including two interceptions.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Sean Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: Tucker didn't garner any touches on offense for the third straight week as Tampa Bay opted to use Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell exclusively in the backfield. Tucker will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as both Irving and Gainwell are available for the Buccaneers.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker didn't record any stats during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Cade Otton
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.
injuryReports.injury: Otton caught one pass for eight yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran wideout ran a team-high 41 routes on Baker Mayfield's 44 dropbacks, but Godwin continues to produce very little with his immense playing time. He's been held under 40 receiving yards in eight straight games and has yet to have a 50-yard receiving game this season. Godwin also has zero touchdowns. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option headed into next Monday night's date with the Panthers.
injuryReports.injury: Godwin caught three passes for 18 yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Ted Hurst III
injuryReports.returnComment: Hurst led the team in targets, and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: Hurst caught five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.

injuryReports.name: Kenny Gainwell
injuryReports.returnComment: Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards and brought in four of five targets for 43 yards in the Buccaneers 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Emeka Egbuka
injuryReports.returnComment: Egbuka couldn't do much despite tying for the second-most targets on the afternoon for the Buccaneers. The 2025 first-round pick's catch total tied his season low, and he also posted his third sub-20-yard tally of the season. Egbuka has now been held under 50 receiving yards in five consecutive contests heading into a Week 12 Monday night home showdown against the Panthers on Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Egbuka brought in two of five targets for 18 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Baker Mayfield
injuryReports.returnComment: Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. Mayfield's rushing yardage total was also a new season high, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' beatable secondary in a Week 12 divisional home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Mayfield completed 20 of 33 passes for 187 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 36 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Tampa Bay.

injuryReports.name: Bucky Irving
injuryReports.returnComment: Irving worked hard all afternoon against a feisty Lions defense, and outside of his game-long 23-yard run, he scuffled to 45 yards on 17 carries. Irving worked around a hard shot to the abdomen that he sustained in the second half, and he did manage to contribute a rushing touchdown for the fourth straight game when he went in from one yard out in the latter portion of the third quarter. Irving has now equaled a career high with eight rushing touchdowns, and he's 107 yards short of his second career 1,000-yard season on the ground heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Irving rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 32 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Yaya Diaby
injuryReports.returnComment: Diaby was inactive in Week 9 due to a knee injury. Now coming off the bye week, the 27-year-old is ready to fit back into his starting linebacker role. He has 16 tackles (11 solo), including 3.0 sacks and two pass breakups, including one interception, through eight regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Diaby is active for Sunday's matchup against Detroit, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Easton Stick
injuryReports.returnComment: The Buccaneers elevated Stick from the team's practice squad Monday. The 31-year-old will only be eligible to play should both Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels exit with an injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Stick (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Lions, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jalon Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Mayfield entered Sunday deemed questionable due to his injuries, but he's ultimately going to be able to suit up. As such, Daniels will retain his role as Mayfield's backup. Easton Stick (coach's decision) is serving as Tampa Bay's emergency third quarterback.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels is set for his usual role as Tampa Bay's backup quarterback Sunday versus Detroit, as Baker Mayfield (foot/thumb) is active and will start, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Josh Hayes
injuryReports.returnComment: Hayes was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, but he is not quite ready to return from a knee procedure that he underwent in late August. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Tykee Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: As a team, the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times Sunday night, but it still wasn't enough to propel Tampa Bay to a win. Smith now has two picks over his last three games and is up to 50 tackles (26 solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. He has a chance to best last season's career-high 100 tackles in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Smith recorded seven tackles (four solo) and an interception in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Zyon McCollum
injuryReports.returnComment: The cornerback has been on an absolute heater in the interceptions department, as he's now recorded at least one pick in three straight games. After picking off Bryce Young and Michael Penix in back-to-back games, McCollum got Caleb Williams twice in Week 9. The four interceptions are a new career high for the fifth-year defensive back, who is now up to 35 tackles (28 solo), 11 pass breakups and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: McCollum recorded five tackles (four solo) and two interceptions in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.

injuryReports.name: Alex Anzalone
injuryReports.returnComment: The Buccaneers picked off Caleb Williams four times, which included Anzalone's pick late in the third quarter that set up Tampa Bay in Chicago territory. Anzalone recorded four interceptions over his first nine NFL seasons, but he's already up to four picks in 2026, three of which have come over his last two outings. He enters the Week 10 bye with 44 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Anzalone posted two solo tackles and an interception during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Daniel Bellinger
injuryReports.returnComment: Bellinger played 26 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. The tight end made the most of his singular target but was primarily utilized as a blocker in the blowout loss.
injuryReports.injury: Bellinger made one catch for five yards in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Xavier Restrepo
injuryReports.returnComment: Even with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) out, Restrepo played as the Titans' WR5 against Dallas, as his 17 offensive snaps trailed all four of Carnell Tate (61), Chimere Dike (53), Elic Ayomanor (36) and Calvin Ridley (26) in terms of playing time. Restrepo played 11 of his 13 snaps on pass plays in the slot, where Robinson operated prior to his injury, but it was actually Dike and Daniel Bellinger who saw the biggest boosts in slot rate with Robinson out.
injuryReports.injury: Restrepo caught his lone target for five yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Michael Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: With Tyjae Spears (knee) back on the shelf and sent to injured reserve over the weekend, Carter played 14 of 68 offensive snaps behind Tony Pollard in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. Carter ended up carrying the ball four times for nine yards and caught is lone target for two yards. He should remain Pollard's backup for at least the next three games while Spears is out unless the Titans have a change of heart and want to start getting rookie Nicholas Singleton some playing time.
injuryReports.injury: Carter reverted to the Titans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Elic Ayomanor
injuryReports.returnComment: Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps were also third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.
injuryReports.injury: Ayomanor caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Joey Slye
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran kicker made field goals from 38, 48 and 28 yards in the first half and is in the midst of a career-best season. He's now 18-for-19 on field-goal tries and has made all 17 PATs through 10 games. Kicking in one of the lower-scoring offenses in the league, it still doesn't translate to much fantasy appeal for Slye ahead of next Sunday's road date with the Jaguars.
injuryReports.injury: Slye made all three field-goal attempts and went 3-for-3 on PATs in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Gunnar Helm
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Helm caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Chimere Dike
injuryReports.returnComment: Dike was able to reel in multiple passes for the third straight game, and his six snags set a new season high for the second-year pro. The 24-year-old paced the team in targets Sunday, narrowly edging out fellow wide receivers Calvin Ridley (six) and Carnell Tate (five). Dike will have a chance to continue carving out a more substantial role for himself on offense moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Dike caught six of seven targets for 69 yards during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Calvin Ridley
injuryReports.returnComment: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Cam Ward
injuryReports.returnComment: Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Ward completed 21 of 30 passes for 248 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for three yards and another score in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Carnell Tate
injuryReports.returnComment: Tate had a fairly non-descript day overall despite the Titans' 30-point output, but he rewarded fantasy managers with a 59-yard catch-and run touchdown in the third quarter on which he alertly got up and ran down the left sideline after Cowboys defenders failed to touch him while he was down. The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Tate has at least 58 receiving yards in five of the last six contests, including in three straight, heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Tate brought in two of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Tony Pollard
injuryReports.returnComment: Pollard eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the third time in the last four games, lighting up his old team for multiple productive gains on the afternoon. The veteran back has been a bright spot in a dismal 1-9 start for Tennessee, despite game script often working against the ground attack in the second halves of the Titans' contests. Pollard remains firmly on pace for a fifth straight 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dan Moore Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Moore may have picked up the injury during the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. James Hudson figures to take over at left tackle in Moore's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Terrell Burgess
injuryReports.returnComment: Burgess injured his knee early in the second half, and he will be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. He was filling in for Tony Adams (illness) at safety, so Isaiah Oliver is the next man up for the Titans.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Cor'Dale Flott
injuryReports.returnComment: Flott was hurt with just under six minutes remaining in the first half while tackling CeeDee Lamb. He was evaluated on the sideline and subsequently deemed questionable to return. Micah Robinson entered at cornerback in Flott's stead.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Tony Adams
injuryReports.returnComment: Adams was added to the Titans' injury report right before the 1 p.m. ET kickoff due to the illness, and the veteran safety wasn't able to take any snaps before being ruled out for Sunday's contest. Terrell Burgess drew the start at safety alongside Kevin Winston in Adams' absence, per Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Nicholas Singleton
injuryReports.returnComment: Week 11 marks the fifth time in six games that Singleton will be a healthy scratch, despite the fact that Tyjae Spears (knee) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. As such, Michael Carter and Julius Chestnut will operate as the Titans' rotational options in the backfield behind workhorse running back Tony Pollard on Sunday. Singleton's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Nov. 29.
injuryReports.injury: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Anthony Hill Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill didn't play in Week 10 against the Jaguars, marking his first absence of the 2026 campaign. He logged a full practice Friday but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation. However, the rookie is cleared to suit up in Week 11 for the meeting with the Cowboys, potentially resulting in fewer snaps for Dorian Mausi.
injuryReports.injury: Hill (neck) is active for Sunday's game against Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Jaylen Harrell
injuryReports.returnComment: Harrell is being monitored following Saturday's accident. The third-year pro tore his ACL in a preseason game against the 49ers in mid-August, which led to him being placed on season-ending injured reserve.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Tyjae Spears
injuryReports.returnComment: Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to be the workhorse running back for the Titans while Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton provide depth out of the backfield.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Kevin Winston Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Winston's practice reps were limited Thursday due to a shoulder issue, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag heading into the weekend. The second-year safety has 56 tackles (31 solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Winston (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuryReports.returnComment: Okonkwo contributed his game-long 32-yard grab on his first catch of the night, and the veteran tight end went on to finish second in receiving yards for the Commanders. Okonkwo also contributed a key 13-yard grab on Washington's penultimate drive that culminated in a key field goal, and in all, three of his four receptions resulted in first downs. Okonkwo has at least four catches in three straight games but is still looking for his first touchdown of the season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Okonkwo brought in four of five targets for 66 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Antonio Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie third-round pick managed new career highs across all three components of his receiving line, which also all served as team-best totals Monday. Williams' last two catches of the night were his most critical, as he recorded 22- and 42-yard grabs to on Washington's final drive to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning 26-yard field goal. Williams hadn't topped 54 receiving yards in any game after a 64-yard effort in his pro debut in Week 1, but Monday night's breakout could serve as a launchpad to a strong stretch run as the Commanders make a playoff push.
injuryReports.injury: Williams brought in nine of 11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Stefon Diggs
injuryReports.returnComment: Diggs finished tied for second on the Commanders in receptions and as the runner-up in targets, although he produced modest yardage with his opportunities. The veteran wideout has at least four catches in seven of the first nine games of his tenure in Washington, and he'll carry a 40-431-6 line into a Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Diggs brought in four of six targets for 45 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Jayden Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, Daniels will look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Daniels completed 23 of 35 passes for 289 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and added six carries for 55 yards in the Commanders' 22-20 win over the Bengals on Monday night.

injuryReports.name: Lucas Patrick
injuryReports.returnComment: Patrick has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in time for Monday night's contest. The starting center is set to defend Jayden Daniels against star Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence.
injuryReports.injury: Patrick (concussion) is active for Monday night's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Amik Robertson
injuryReports.returnComment: Robertson suffered an ankle injury at the team's final practice of the week, so his absence Monday comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Sainristil and Quan Martin will both likely operate in more prominent roles at cornerback versus Cincinnati.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Rachaad White
injuryReports.returnComment: White showed up on the Commanders' Week 11 injury report Friday as limited due to a heel issue and then didn't practice Saturday, leaving him questionable to play Monday. While he's confirmed to be available, he also will be welcoming back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) from IR for the first time since Week 5, which may eat into White's workload.
injuryReports.injury: White (heel) is active for Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
injuryReports.returnComment: Croskey-Merritt will make his return to the Commanders' 53-man roster after he spent the minimum four games on IR while recovering from the groin injury. Considering that he was a full practice participant throughout Week 11 in addition to the uncertain status of complementary back Rachaad White (questionable, heel), Croskey-Merritt could return to a lead role out of the Washington backfield right away. Prior to landing on IR, Croskey-Merritt led Washington in rushing (67 carries for 239 yards and two touchdowns) while adding five receptions for 40 yards over the team's first five games.
injuryReports.injury: The Commanders activated Croskey-Merritt (groin) from injured reserve and removed his designation ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Quan Martin
injuryReports.returnComment: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.
injuryReports.injury: Martin (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Treylon Burks
injuryReports.returnComment: Burks was held out of Friday's practice while managing a foot injury, but he returned Saturday as a full participant, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Monday's contest. Over his last six outings, Burks has caught 14 passes on 24 targets for 260 yards and two touchdowns, and he has operated as operated as the Commanders' WR3 since Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6 against the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: Burks (foot) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Laremy Tunsil
injuryReports.returnComment: Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
injuryReports.injury: Triceps

injuryReports.name: Colson Yankoff
injuryReports.returnComment: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.
injuryReports.injury: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Luke McCaffrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.
injuryReports.injury: McCaffrey returned two punts for 13 yards and three kickoffs for 58 yards in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Reaves
injuryReports.returnComment: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.
injuryReports.injury: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nick Cross
injuryReports.returnComment: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.
injuryReports.injury: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).

injuryReports.name: Frankie Luvu
injuryReports.returnComment: Luvu stopped the Giants' red zone drive in the third quarter after punching the ball out of the hands of Malik Nabers, and Jeremy Reaves jumped on the loose ball to secure the takeaway for the Commanders. Luvu has played every single snap in each of his last three games, and he has accumulated 51 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery over his last six outings.
injuryReports.injury: Luvu recorded six tackles (two solo) and a forced fumble during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Sonny Styles
injuryReports.returnComment: Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).
injuryReports.injury: Styles recorded 13 tackles (five solo) during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Drew Stevens
injuryReports.returnComment: Stevens began the scoring in the contest with a 46-yard field goal early in the second period. That ended up being his only FG try of the game, but he made all three of his PATs. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.
injuryReports.injury: Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Ben Sinnott
injuryReports.returnComment: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.
injuryReports.injury: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.

injuryReports.name: Austin Ekeler
injuryReports.returnComment: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.
injuryReports.injury: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

sources.returnComment: Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. He added 19 yards on four carries. The 28-year-old does have some starting experience -- he helmed the Giants' offense for eight starts between 2023 and 2024 -- but didn't play at all in 2025. For now, the Patriots are at least communicating that they'll stand pat and not look for help at quarterback outside the organization. However, the team is barely hanging on in the AFC playoff race with a 5-5 record, and with only rookie Behren Morton on the active roster as a healthy option to DeVito, the team may still look elsewhere if DeVito is unable to show better production moving forward.
sources.injury: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that DeVito is the team's starting quarterback, Mike Reiss of ESPN reports. "We're excited about that. He had a good preseason and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said of DeVito.

tdReport.orderMethodology: First and last TD fair odds come from separate player-game models trained on actual first/last scorer IDs, including defensive/return TDs in the event order and overtime. They use lagged opportunity and prior scoring-order rates; ATTD probabilities are not reused as first/last estimates. Game-level probability caps reserve mass for unmodeled scorers and no-TD outcomes. Book settlement rules may differ.
